runs.t: Dropzone Commander uses six-sided dice referred to as
D6
. Most rolls require a specific number or better to succeed and will usually be written without the ‘D6’, i.e., if a player needs to roll at least a 5 on a D6, that’s a 5+.
You will often need to roll multiple D6, sometimes written as X D6, with X being the number of dice to roll.
If you’re required to roll a three-sided dice—a D3—simulate it using a D6 (1 or 2 = 1, 3 or 4 = 2, 5 or 6 = 3).
Some rules allow you to re-roll dice. Roll the dice again and apply the second result, even if it is worse.
Dice can only be re-rolled once.
Modifiers may be applied to dice rolls.
Modifiers that improve a dice roll will make it more likely.
For example, a 4+ roll which gains a +1 modifier becomes a 3+ roll.
Modifiers that worsen a dice roll will make it less likely.
For example, a 4+ roll that suffers a -1 modifier becomes a 5+ roll.
Modifiers applied to a dice roll cannot make it impossible or certain.
After all modifiers are applied, stop at the minimum/maximum value e.g. a 6+ or 2+ on a D6.
Modifiers are usually written in shorthand: ‘suffers -2Ac’ is a -2 modifier to its Ac value.
Modifiers to numbers which aren’t dice rolls are applied mathematically (a -2 modifier will reduce an 8 to 6). Numbers can be reduced to a minimum of 0.
Division and multiplication are applied together after all other modifiers are applied.
If a distance is divided, the result is rounded down to the nearest half inch. If anything else is divided, the result is rounded down.
Modifiers do not persist after the rule that applied them no longer applies. Multiple modifiers have a cumulative effect.

If anything gains a duplicate stat, use the better one. If the duplicate is random, e.g. D6, use its maximum possible outcome to determine if it replaces an existing stat. Other modifiers are applied after a duplicate stat is gained.
If something receives a modifier to a special rule it does not have, it gains that special rule while the modifier applies. For example, if a Unit without Ev (Evasion) gains +2Ev, it gains Ev2.
A stat with no numerical value cannot be modified.
Dropzone uses inches, so players need a tape measure or ruler marked in inches. Shorthand for inches is used: 12” means 12 inches.
You may pre-measure distances at any time—your crews have the sensors of a future universe on hand.
These core rules should be accessible for reference. Players should also have copies of any relevant stats.
A special rule overrides a core rule.

Rarely, obscure rules conflicts and situations are not addressed. If re-reading the relevant rules section does not provide an answer, and the players cannot agree, have one player roll a D6. On a 1-3 one interpretation is correct, on a 4-6 it is the other.
Each player’s Army is represented by individual Unit miniatures. Their rules are covered in the next section.
Tokens represent various statuses and effects. If you use a non-standard token to represent anything, state what it represents.
These must be 20mm in diameter since these are the only Tokens whose exact placement matters. Distances may be measured to/from any point on Object Tokens.

Dropzone is played on a 48”x48” gaming area referred to as the Table. For particularly large or small games, you may want to alter this size. You will need extra space for Units yet to enter play, unused dice, and other game components.
All distances are measured parallel to the Table surface.
Anything in play is ‘on the Table’, including Units aboard Transports.

Ground is what your Units move over (or not), including roads, fields, and rivers. Ground can be 3D, including hills and cliffs, but should be a practical gaming surface. Avoid long inclines, large expanses of deep texture, and awkward details.
Zones are removable scenery models which can be Occupied by Infantry Units. These are either Buildings or Areas like forests, ruins, or barricaded redoubts.
Zones can be destroyed and sometimes have destructible Features which may be represented by Tokens or removable parts.
Distances measured to/from Zones may be measured from any point on them. If a rule states a Zone should be ‘within’ anything, any point is used to determine this.
Units are individual Vehicle, Aircraft, and Infantry miniatures. An Infantry Unit is 1 or more figures permanently affixed to a 17x35mm base. Legacy 22x45mm bases are acceptable.
An Aircraft sits on a flight stand which must be of stock size and height, as indicated on its stat sheet, and the miniature must be supported by it alone.
Your Units are friendly Units. Your opponent’s Units are enemy Units.
Certain rules specify friendly or enemy Units, or may not specify either, in which case both can be affected.
Destroyed Units are removed from play.

All distances are measured to/from a Unit’s centre. A Vehicle’s centre sits on the top of the miniature’s hull. An Aircraft’s centre is where its flight stand’s stem meets the miniature. An Infantry Unit’s centre is the middle of its base.
If a rule states a Unit should be ‘within’ anything, its centre is used to determine this.
You cannot measure to or from a Unit aboard a Transport. Therefore, many actions, such as targeting them with Weapons, are not possible.
A Unit’s stats sheet includes a thumbnail indicating its centre:

body.alt: A tank with its centre marked by a red dot.

runs.t: Placing a Unit is letting it stand freely after moving it or putting it on the Table.
Units may only be placed where they fit stably, realistically, and wholly on the Table—no balancing tanks at 45-degrees against a wall!

Units cannot overlap, and flight stands cannot overlap. You cannot move one to overlap with another if it’s possible not to. If a rule would force one to overlap with another, the moved Unit’s player must shift their Unit so that they are in contact but not overlapping if there’s no alternative.

Vehicle and Infantry Units MAY be placed on top of a flight stand’s base. If an Aircraft is placed above a Vehicle or Infantry Unit, place that Unit in the same location on top of the Aircraft’s flight stand’s base if necessary. The flight stand’s stem may not be deliberately placed on top of any Unit.
Units may be placed on top of Tokens. If you’re using a premium, 3D version of a Token, substitute it for a 2D one if needed.
If a Unit is placed illegitimately or on scenery it must move around, it is destroyed.
Units operate together in Squads. Many rules refer to using Squads rather than Units. A Squad with one Unit is still a Squad. If a Squad receives a modifier, every Unit in it receives it.

A Group is normally one Squad and, often, a Squad of Transports to carry it. Squads within Groups operate together, and many rules refer to using Groups rather than Squads. A Group with one Squad is still a Group. If a Group receives a modifier, every Unit in it receives it.
Each Unit has a stats bar:

items.t: : How many may form a Squad and what category it is.
: How much it costs to field.
: The Unit’s type—either a Vehicle, Aircraft, or Infantry.
: How well protected it is physically.
: The amount of damage it can take before being destroyed.

runs.t: Infantry have an
Offence (OF)
stat, representing their lethality against Infantry up close. They also have a
Defence (DF)
stat instead of an Armour value, representing their skill at surviving certain situations.
Infantry also have a
Bravery (B)
stat. If an Infantry Squad/Unit needs to take a Bravery Test, roll 1D6 against its B stat. If it has a B value of ‘A’, it passes automatically.
If a Unit, or a Unit’s special rule, has a random stat, determine this once each time it is used. All Units in the Squad with that stat use that result.
Most Units have Weapons. A Weapon’s capabilities are described in its profile:

items.t: : The direction/s in which it may attack.
: The maximum distance its Unit may move and still attack with this Weapon. If it may move its full distance, this value is ‘Full’.
: Its range. If it has two values, the second is used against Vehicles and Aircraft to represent their active countermeasures destroying incoming munitions.
: The number of dice it attacks with.
: How accurate it is. Weapons with an Ac value of A hit automatically.

runs.t: If a Weapon, or a Weapon’s special rule, has a random stat, determine this each time it is applied, e.g. if it has 2 Attacks, Energy D6, roll for each attack as it attempts to damage.
First, decide the game’s size and points limit within the margins below. Each game size dictates the maximum number of Groups your Army may contain:
Skirmish
: 501–1000 points. 9 Groups Max.
Clash
: 1001–2000 points. 12 Groups Max.
Battle
: 2001–3000 points. 16 Groups Max.
Reconquest
: 3001 points and above. 20 Groups Max but add 4 Groups to the maximum allowed for every 1000pts above 3000.
Building your Army is as simple as building around Standard category Units, keeping within the game’s points and Groups limits, and meeting these restrictions:
Lastly,
no Group may cost more than 1/4 of your total allowed pts.

These are indicated by ‘Rare’ or ‘Unique’ besides their points cost. You may only take one Rare Squad with the same name in a Skirmish, two in a Clash, and three in a Battle/Reconquest. You may only take one Unique Squad with the same name.
Some Squads have Variants—options for different Weapon loadouts or special rules.
A Weapon with an orange-highlighted name box will only be used by certain Variants—that Variant’s name will be shown in brackets after the Weapon’s.
Special rules which only apply to certain Variants will be indicated in brackets after the rule.
A Squad may contain any mixture of Variants.
Some Units offer Weapons upgrades. These Weapons have green-highlighted name boxes including the points cost of the upgrade.
Some Weapon upgrades will replace existing Weapons. The stats sheet will state which.
All Units of the same Variant within a Squad must be upgraded equally.

Units with the category ‘Transport’ may only be chosen along with a Squad they may transport. Transports do not have a minimum or maximum Squad size—you may take as many identical Transports as needed to carry their Squad. Those Transport(s) form a Squad. Those two Squads form one Group.

Transports must be taken full, and a Squad must have enough Transports for all its Units. Squads with Transports begin the game aboard them. You may take Squads without Transports, but this can affect when they can join the battle (see page 34 ‘Entry’).
Up to 4 Squads, plus their Transport Squads if they have any, may all share ONE Transport. These all form one Group.
Group 1:
Single Squad, no Transport.
Group 2:
Single Squad entirely filling a single Transport.
Group 3:
Single Squad filling multiple identical Transports.
Group 4:
One or more Squads in (but not necessarily filling) a single Auxiliary Transport Squad.
Group 5:
Up to 4 different Squads (with their filled Transports if applicable) filling one larger Transport.

runs.t: Transports and Units which can be transported have a Transport Symbol.
A Transport’s Symbol is hollow. Its shape abstractly represents what Units it can carry. A number inside that Symbol shows how much it can carry.
A Unit which can be transported has a solid Symbol matching the Transports that can carry it. A number inside that Symbol shows how much space it fills.
Transports which can be carried by a larger Transport will have both types of Symbol.
Transports may only carry Units with the same shaped Symbol as itself ( and ) and may not carry more than their number indicates.
If carrying another Transport, the cargo of the smaller Transport is ignored (they are already aboard).

A Transport with two hollow Symbols separated by a /, e.g.  / , may not carry a mix of those Symbol shapes (in this case, either all solid squares or all solid triangles). A Transport with two hollow Symbols separated by a +, e.g.  + , may carry both simultaneously. A Unit with two solid Symbols separated by a /, e.g. / , may use either.

runs.t: Units with a hollow Transport Symbol which are not of the category ‘Transport’ are Auxiliary Transports—these are taken like normal Squads. Auxiliary Transports do not have to be full. Any Squad/s which the Auxiliary Transports do carry join the Auxiliary Transports’ Group. A carried Squad cannot be split between multiple Auxiliary Transport Squads.
You must take at least one Commander from the table below or from your faction’s Famous Commanders:

Commanders must be assigned to a Unit when building your Army. Squads can only contain one Commander. Famous Commanders are automatically assigned a Unit in their profile. The Commander’s points combine with that Unit’s points during games but are ignored during Army composition besides counting towards your total allowed points.
If the Unit a Commander is assigned to is destroyed, that Commander is killed.
Command Cards represent special actions made by Commanders. They are optional in Skirmish-size games. Otherwise, players must build their decks before playing.

All players have access to a 33-card Core Set. By agreement, players can use this as-is when learning to play. Otherwise, each player constructs a deck of 45 cards from a combination of this Core Set and their faction’s 33-card Faction Set. Players may not, for example, take cards from two Core Sets. To check this, all cards have a number in the bottom-left corner: the maximum number of copies of this card your deck can contain.
For casual games, players may simply combine both Sets to make a 66-card deck.
Famous Commanders, narrative events, special Armies, and some miniatures may include Special Command Cards to supplement a player’s pool of available cards.
Shuffle your deck before each game and place it face-down.
Every military action has objectives. Scenarios define how the Table should look, how your Units approach it, how long the game is, and how to win.
Choose a Scenario before each game once players have built their Armies—this avoids unbalanced Armies designed to tackle a specific Scenario.

Dropzone Commander is played over several Rounds, with each split into Phases. During a Round, players must follow each Phase and any steps within it in order. Once all Phases have been completed, the game advances to the next Round.
This is a quick summary of how to play each Round. Terms you are not yet familiar with will be covered later.
Players generate/replenish their Command Points (CP) up to a number equal to their highest Commander Level on the Table. Players lose CP here if they have more than that.
Commanders count as Level 0 throughout Round 1.

If a player has two fewer Groups on the Table/Ready to enter it than their opponent, they generate a Pass token. For each additional Group fewer than their opponent, they generate another Pass token. Groups which contain only non-auxiliary Transports are ignored when generating Pass tokens.

Players may find it useful to keep a stack of Activation tokens equal to their available Groups to help calculate if any Pass tokens are needed. Activation tokens can later be placed onto activated Groups as reminders.
Each Player may discard any unwanted Command Cards face-up.

Each player may draw/replenish their hand of Command Cards up to a number of cards equal to their highest Commander Level on the Table. Players must discard cards here if they have more than that. Keep your hand hidden from your opponent.
If you have no cards remaining in your deck, you cannot draw more cards.

Each player rolls a D6 and adds the level of their highest level Commander on the Table. A roll of 6 wins automatically, but if both players roll 6s, add their Commander Level as normal. Re-roll any ties after adding the Commander Level. The winner has the Initiative until the next Round.

The player with the Initiative either picks one of their Groups on the Table or one that’s Ready to enter, or they can force their opponent to instead. Groups containing only non-auxiliary Transports cannot be picked.
That player completes that Group’s activation.
A player may use a Pass token instead of activating a Group. Choosing not to move a Ready Group onto the Table is also a pass—it counts as activated.
Once that player has completed that activation, the next player activates one of their Groups.
Once all Groups which may activate normally have done so, discard any remaining Pass tokens.

The player with the Initiative activates all their un-activated Groups containing only non-auxiliary Transports as if they were one Group, or they can force their opponent to instead. The other player then activates all of theirs.
See page 32 ‘Weapon Features’.
If the Scenario awards Victory Points at the end of this Round, award them now.
Various rules take effect.
Various rules take effect, and the Round ends.
Players can use Abilities which cost CP to perform. Players may use each Ability once per Round. Players have access to 3 core Abilities:

r.t: . At the start of the Initiation Phase, if all your Commanders have been killed, place a L3 Commander on any friendly Unit on the Table. That Commander is worth 0pts.
. On the activation of a friendly Group, if it does not have enough Transports, you may Reassign another to it.

Pick one of your empty Transports which has not yet activated this Round and is not aboard another Transport. That Transport leaves its original Group and joins the active Group. It must be able to Transport all/some of the Units in its new Group. You may not Reassign Auxiliary Transports.

. At the end of the Round, look at the top X cards of your Command Card deck and return some/all of them to the top of your deck in any order. Place any remaining ones on the bottom of your deck in any order.

runs.t: Famous Commanders may grant players additional Abilities. These may only be used while their respective Commander is on the Table, but if that Commander is killed or leaves the Table, any effects of previously used Abilities persist.
Command Cards are set out as follows:

body.alt: An example Command Card: HQ Directive.

runs.t: Name
: The card’s name.
Cost

: Its cost in CP, paid when the card takes effect. If a second, red cost is present, it may be paid instead to Boost the card. If you don’t/can’t pay its cost, the card fails to take effect. If a card is prevented from taking effect, no CP is due.
Radius

: How far from one of your Commanders its target may be. Infantry inside Zones can be targeted if the Zone is within this. Cards with no Radius value can target anything, even if it’s not on the Table.
Play
: When it can be played.
Target
: Its allowed target/s. If the target is a Group or Squad, only one Unit within it needs to be targeted.
Effect
: The effect it has. This lasts until the end of the Round unless otherwise stated. If this creates Units, Features, or Tokens, those remain.
BOOST
: If a red CP cost was paid, the card is modified as described.
Players may only play Command Cards if they have a Commander on the Table. Players may play as many cards from their hand as they like during a Round.
To play a card, follow its rules. Sometimes, the sequencing of multiple cards played at the same time matters (see page 17 ‘The Stack’).
Played and discarded cards are placed face-up on their player’s discard pile.
Command Cards with gold outer borders cannot be prevented from taking effect.

If a Command Card requires a Unit have a special rule or not have a special rule (e.g. if it Effects Units with Assault, or it Targets Units without UC), that Unit must have that special rule natively on its stats sheet.
Each card has a helpful symbol indicating roughly when it can be played:
When cards are played at the same ‘Play’ requirement (e.g. the end of the Initiation Phase) or in response to other cards, they form a Stack which determines the order they resolve.

When you play a card, announce you’re doing so and declare it’s ‘Play’ requirement. Before your opponent sees it, they may announce cards that may be played then, and you may do the same. Once all cards are announced, the player without the Initiative reveals one, declares its Target, and places it on the Stack. Next, the player with Initiative does the same until all played cards are revealed.

Next, players may announce more cards that may be played then. As above, reveal them, declare their targets, then place them on the Stack. Continue until both players have played all the cards they want to.
Now resolve all the cards’ effects, starting with the highest in the Stack. Further cards cannot be played until these have resolved.
Players may wait until the Stack resolves before playing more cards, starting a new Stack.
One revealed card is still a Stack.

When a Group is activated, each Squad within it may move and then attack, or attack and then move. Units may choose not to attack. Units outside Transports and Zones which have not moved make a 0” move at the end of their activation.

Squads within a Group are moved one Squad at a time, either before or after attacking, but all must attack simultaneously. For example, a Squad of Tanks could move, attack with their Dropship, and then their Dropship could move.
Squads within Groups do not have to stay near each other.
Once a Group completes these steps, its activation is over.

Move every Unit within the Squad up to its maximum Mv, or if it has attacked this Round, the lowest MA of any Weapon it attacked with. If the Unit moves around anything, the real distance is measured. Units may turn freely while moving but pivoting on the spot counts as moving 1”.

Units may move through Infantry, Aircraft, and friendly Units but must move around Zones and enemy Vehicles. In an exception to the Placing Units rules, Vehicles may end their move overlapping Infantry—the Infantry must then be shifted the minimum possible distance by their player, maintaining coherency.
Aircraft can move over anything, but no Unit may end its move on top of a Zone.

body.alt: Measure all distances from centre to centre

runs.t: Units must maintain a coherency of 3”—the maximum distance one may be from at least one other Unit in its Squad. A Squad of one Unit is always in coherency. Units inside the same Zone count as within 3” of each other. Units aboard Transports are always in coherency.
You may not end a Squad’s movement with Unit/s out of coherency if it’s possible not to.
A Squad cannot have more than one set of Units outside Transports in coherency. If it would, pick one set to be in Coherency. All other Units outside Transports in that Squad are out of coherency.
A Squad may not attack if any of its Units are out of coherency.
Units can only be in coherency with others in their Squad.
Ground is all scenery that isn’t Zones—generally the contours of the playing surface. Ground quality can affect movement.
Exceptional
—roads, tarmac. Vehicles gain +2”Mv if they spend their entire move with the whole miniature on this Ground (not including moves while aboard a Transport).
Good
—hard soil, smooth rock, pavement, cracked tarmac, flat ice, compacted sand. No restriction to movement.
Poor
—deep snow, marshes, bogs, shallow water, uneven surfaces. Vehicles and Infantry must use 2” of their available Mv for every 1” crossed.
Impassable
—quicksand, deep water, lava, acid fields. Infantry and Vehicles must move around this.
Most of the Table should be Good Ground. Clearly define any other Ground.
Ground also includes any non-Zone details—like boulders, street furniture, and car wrecks—that protrude from the gaming surface.

Vehicles and Infantry must move around anything they couldn’t realistically move over. Use reasonable judgement—a tank won’t be stopped by a wooden fence, but it couldn’t move over concrete tank traps.
Vehicles and Infantry cannot move up or down an incline above 45 degrees. Small ‘steps up’, like curbs, can be moved over—again, use reasonable judgement.
You may attack with Weapons with a MA equal to or less than the distance its Unit has moved this Round. To attack, follow this sequence:

items.t: Total attacks and roll to hit

runs.t: NB: Since players may pre-measure, steps 1 and 2 are completed simultaneously.
Targets may be Units or Zones. You may not target friendly Units.
Only Weapons with the AA (Anti-Air) special rule may target Aircraft.
Potential targets must be in range

. Use the Weapon’s R value. If it has two R values, use the second against Vehicles and Aircraft. For Weapons with a R of ‘CC’, any part of the attacking miniature or its base/flight stand must be touching any part of the target miniature or its base/flight stand.
Potential targets must lie within a Weapon’s arc

, measured as 90-degree wedges from the centre of the attacking Unit’s main body/base. Arcs are Front (F), Side (S) and Rear (R). Side arcs are sometimes restricted to Side Left (SL) or Side Right (SR). If the target is on the line between Arcs, the attacker must decide which Arc it is in for that attack. Units cannot be in more than one Arc.
Potential targets must be in Clear or Obscured Line of Sight.
Units and Scenery obstruct Line of Sight, except Aircraft flight stands and Infantry.

A Unit has Clear Line of Sight to another if an unobstructed straight line can be drawn between their centres (these two Units themselves do not obstruct this line). If a Unit is sat on another’s flight stand, measure as if the flight stand wasn’t there.
A Unit has Obscured Line of Sight if the line can be drawn to any part of the target, excluding gun barrels, but not its centre.
The Sabre has Obscured Line of Sight to the Drones as a straight line cannot be drawn from the centre of the Sabre to the centre of the Drones’ base.
A Unit may draw Line of Sight through other Units in its own Squad. If doing so, the target is Obscured.
The Tusk is Obscured to Polecat 1 as it must draw Line of Sight through its squadmate, Polecat 2. Polecat 2 has Clear Line of Sight to the Tusk.
Line of Sight can be measured to/from any point on a Zone. If checking range to/from a Zone while checking Line of Sight, use this same point.
Do not build models unfairly, i.e., by lengthening a walker’s legs or assembling it crouched ultra-low. It’s not cool.
Players should not re-pose models mid-game, and Aircraft should be posed at/near level flight on their stands—Aircraft banked at 90-degrees are modelled for advantage.
You must assign a target for every attacking Weapon within a Group before rolling any dice.

children.heading: Total Attacks and Roll to Hit

runs.t: Assign attacks to each target equal to each Weapon’s Att.
Roll a D6 for each attack—results of at least the Weapons’ Ac hit.
Weapons attacking Obscured targets suffer -2Ac.
Against Infantry, each hit inflicts 1DP without rolling to inflict damage.
E0 hits cannot inflict damage, including against Infantry.

Otherwise, for each hit, use the Energy vs Armour table below to determine the roll required to inflict damage. Here, treat values above 10 as 10. Note that damage here is never certain, but sometimes impossible.
Each success inflicts 1 damage—the target loses 1 DP. If the result is at least 2 higher than the required roll, that result is a
Critical
—another 1 damage is inflicted. Since you do not roll to inflict damage against Infantry, they cannot receive Criticals.
Also roll against this table for hits from other sources e.g. Command Cards.
When a target is reduced to 0DP, it is destroyed. Any additional damage is ignored.
Record lost DP on surviving targets using dice or tokens.

When a Transport is destroyed, Units aboard are destroyed on a 5+ (roll for each Unit). Do not roll for Units aboard a Transport aboard the destroyed Transport, but if a Transport is destroyed by this roll, then roll for its contents.

Survivors must be placed within 3” of the original destroyed Transport and, if possible, in coherency—Infantry must be placed within 2”. They may still activate and use their full Mv but may not attack later that Round.
When an Aircraft with an initial DP of 2-4 is destroyed, Vehicles and Zones within 2” suffer an E5 hit. Each Infantry Unit within 2” is destroyed on a 4+.
When an Aircraft with an initial DP of 5 or more is destroyed, Vehicles and Zones within 2” suffer 2 E5 hits. Each Infantry Unit within 2” is destroyed on a 3+.
If the destroyed Aircraft had Units aboard, place any survivors after resolving these hits.
Weapons with the AA special rule are anti-air Weapons.
Only AA Weapons can target Aircraft normally. AA Weapons ignore the Ev (Evasion) special rule on non-Aircraft.

When an enemy Aircraft completes its move, and if, during its move, it passed within range and Line of Sight of an AA Weapon which has not attacked this Round and may attack, you may declare a Reaction Attack. A Unit that moves 0” has still moved.
Target where the top of the Aircraft’s flight stand would be from Ground level, or above the roof of a Building, at that point during its movement.

The Weapon immediately attacks the enemy Aircraft, suffering -2 Ac. It must follow the normal rules and attacking limits, so it may not usually attack again later that Round, although its Unit may attack with other Weapons if/when it activates.
If the Aircraft is destroyed, it is destroyed at the targeted point.

Multiple Weapons may Reaction Attack the same Aircraft—declare and resolve each individually, so if you’re unsuccessful, you can attack with the next qualifying Weapon. The next Weapon must target the same point or a point further along that Aircraft’s movement.
Anti-Air Reactive (AA-R) Weapons may only Reaction Attack but suffer no penalty for doing so. Anti-Air Slow (AA-S) Weapons may not Reaction Attack.
Small Arms Weapons have an E value of ‘S’ followed by a number. They can only damage Infantry—each hit inflicts 1DP without rolling to inflict damage.
Obscured Infantry may roll against their DF value to block each Small Arms hit.

However, against Vehicles or Aircraft, 5 attacks from Small Arms Weapons, which may come from multiple Units, can be combined into a single attack of an E value equal to the lowest number after ‘S’ from these attacks. For example, six S2 attacks and four S3 attacks could be combined into two energy 2 attacks. These are no longer Small Arms attacks. Use the worst Ac, after any modifiers, from these attacks for the combined attack. Except ‘Alt’, ‘Ineffective’, and ‘Strafe’, any special rules those Weapons have are ignored for the combined attack if they do not all share that special rule.
Energy modifiers to Small Arms Weapons only affect their combined attack/s—apply the worst modifier among the combining attacks.
Other sources may inflict Small Arms hits—these cannot be combined.

Aircraft can be vulnerable to massed, handheld gunfire. Non-AA Small Arms Weapons carried by Infantry may target Aircraft within 9” if their R permits. These attacks may be combined. They may not Reaction Attack.
AA Small Arms Weapons use their full R values, and multiple examples may Reaction Attack simultaneously.

Many sources deal damage/hits to an Infantry Squad, not individual Units within it. When this happens, damage is dealt to that Squad’s most damaged Unit until it is destroyed, then to the next Unit of their player’s choice. If two Units begin equally damaged, their player chooses which to damage. Any remaining damage against destroyed Squads is discarded.
Weapons targeting a Vehicle or Aircraft containing a Commander that’s in coherency with at least 1 other Unit suffer -1Ac.
If an Infantry Unit containing a Commander is destroyed, that Commander may transfer to another Unit in coherency.
Some special rules place Status Tokens. These indicate special effects to the Squad they are placed on.

You may only place one of the same type of Status Token during a Group’s activation. If something, e.g. one of your Blast Weapons, might place Status Tokens on multiple Squads, you choose which Squad receives one.
Remove any Status Tokens on a Squad at the end of its activation unless they were placed that activation.
If Units exit a Transport, they and the Transport have each completed a Disembark operation—the Units Disembark from the Transport, the Transport Disembarks the Units.
If Units enter a Transport, they and the Transport have each completed an Embark operation—the Units Embark into the Transport, the Transport Embarks the Units.
Units which Embark or Disembark may not move more than half their Mv that activation.
Units may Embark or Disembark at any time during their activation.

Embarking/Disembarking is not a move. A Transport could move, attack, then Embark Units. It could also move a bit, Disembark Units, then continue to move. However, Units may not split their move before/after Embarking or Disembarking into or from a Transport.
Units may not attack in the same Round as Embarking or Disembarking from a Transport.

runs.t: Disembarked Units must be placed within 3” of their Transport—Infantry must be placed within 2”. All Units aboard Transports within a Squad must Disembark simultaneously and into coherency with the full Squad, or those Units can’t Disembark.
Units may not Disembark from a Transport Aircraft if it is within 3” of an enemy Vehicle.

When Embarking, every Unit in the Squad must be within 3” of their Transport/s—Infantry must be within 2”. All Units not aboard Transports in the Squad must Embark simultaneously, or those Units can’t Embark.
Units may not Embark into a Transport Aircraft if it is within 3” of an enemy Vehicle.
No Unit may complete more than two Embark and/or Disembark operations per Round. Placing Units after their Transport has been destroyed is not Disembarking.

Units aboard a Transport that is Embarking/Disembarking from a larger Transport (e.g. Infantry aboard an APC aboard a Dropship) use up one of these operations as well when their Transport Embarks or Disembarks. For example, an APC could Disembark from a Dropship and then the Infantry aboard the APC could Disembark from it—1 operation for the Dropship, 2 for the APC, 2 for the Infantry. The APC could not Embark into a Dropship, Disembark, and then Disembark its Infantry—that would be 3 operations for the APC and the Infantry.
Squads within Groups do not have to Embark or Disembark together, but their Transport can still only complete 2 Embark/Disembark operations per Round.

Embarking or Disembarking multiple Squads simultaneously is a single operation. For example, a Dropship could Disembark two Squads in two separate places (2 operations) or Embark both in one place then Disembark both in another (2 operations). It could not Embark them in separate places then Disembark them in separate places (4 operations).

A Unit cannot Disembark from a Transport Vehicle if scenery it cannot move over lies between the point it would be placed and that Transport Vehicle. A Unit cannot Embark into a Transport Vehicle if scenery it cannot move over lies between the point it would Embark from and that Transport Vehicle.
Zones are scenery pieces that Units can interact with, and Infantry can Occupy. They are either Buildings or Areas.
Zones cannot be moved but can be destroyed.
Scenarios will specify which to use and where to place them. Most specify standard sizes:
Zones can be any size and height—the example images are guidelines—but players must define which profile all Zones have before playing.
Buildings should be fully enclosed with at least three faces—straight walls are best. In unclear examples, like a round tower, divide it visually into faces.
Flat roofs with plenty of room to place Infantry are recommended—you’ll see why shortly.
Areas are dense regions, typically forests, boulder fields, ruins, and barricaded redoubts. Areas should have a clearly defined edge, so are best modelled onto a base.
It’s helpful to leave at least 1” of mostly flat base around the edge of an Area—deep enough to place Infantry.

Since Areas often feature foliage and other ambiguous forms, they are an exception to the normal Line of Sight rules. Line of Sight may be drawn through up to 3” total of one of more Areas, in which case the target is Obscured. Areas are infinitely high for Line of Sight purposes but are ignored when drawing Line of Sight to/from Aircraft, Buildings, and Sited Squads inside Buildings.
Given these rules, using 2D templates for Areas is acceptable.

Infantry may enter/exit Zones via their Entrances: the edges of Areas, or the doors and windows of Buildings. Entering is Embarking, exiting is Disembarking—treat the Zone as a Transport. Zones however have no Embark/Disembark limit, and Transport symbols are ignored.
Once Infantry have entered, indicate their presence inside using tokens or by placing the models centrally on a Building’s roof/inside an Area. They now Occupy the Zone and are Occupiers.
Infantry may also enter a Zone directly from a Transport if it is within 1” of an Entrance. This is a single Disembark/Embark for the Infantry.
Infantry may not re-enter a Zone in the same Round as exiting it.
Players Control a Zone if their Infantry Occupied it while it was empty, or if only they have Occupiers.
Players Contest a Zone if their Infantry Occupied it while enemies were already inside.
Squads gain +1B if their player Controls the Zone they are Occupying.

runs.t: Infantry may not voluntarily exit a Zone in the same Round as entering it.

Your Infantry may not exit a Zone unless you have more Occupying Units in it than your opponent. If you have more Occupying Units, take a Bravery Test for each of your Occupying Squads when they activate. At least one Squad which passes may exit, but beyond that you must leave at least 1 Unit per enemy Unit inside.
When exiting, if it’s impossible for every Unit to be placed within 2” of an Entrance, e.g. from a bunker with only one door, then they must be as close as possible to it.
Infantry may also exit a Zone directly into a Transport if it is within 1” of an Entrance. This is a single Disembark/Embark for the Infantry.
Infantry may transfer from one Zone into another which touches it. This is still exiting, but costs one Disembark and one Embark.
Weapons always hit Zones on a 2+. This cannot be modified, even by special rules. Weapons with an Ac value of A hit Zones automatically.
Criticals do not inflict additional damage against Zones.
Players may target Zones containing friendly Infantry.
For each DP inflicted against a Building, or 2DP inflicted against an Area, each Occupying Squad suffers one Small Arms hit. Squads gain +1DF against these hits if no enemies Occupy that Zone.
When a Zone is reduced to 0DP, it is destroyed. Any additional damage is ignored—extra collateral damage is not inflicted.
Destroyed Areas are removed. Each Occupying Unit is destroyed on a 4+. Players must place their survivors in coherency within the space where the Area was.

Destroyed Buildings are replaced by an Area of identical size with 10DP, A2, representing the ruins. Outside, Vehicles and Infantry within 2” of the Building suffer D6-2 damage. Inside, each Occupying Unit is destroyed on a 2+. Survivors now Occupy the Area as before.

children.heading: Siting Occupiers and Attacking from Zones

runs.t: Occupiers may only attack if Sited.

First, when a Squad enters a Zone or activates inside one, you may Site it. Indicate where each Squad is Sited using tokens or, preferably, the miniatures, by placing that Squad against a single face with windows or doors (for Buildings) or a single edge point (for Areas). Miniatures can overlap here since they are just functioning as markers. This is not moving.
A friendly Squad Occupying a Zone you Contest must pass a Bravery test to be Sited.
Squads automatically un-Site at the beginning of their activation but may immediately re-Site. Once Sited, a Squad cannot un-Site or exit the Zone that Round unless forced to.

When attacking from a Building, Line of Sight and range may be measured from any window or door on the face that Squad is Sited on, excluding its corners (use the same point for both). Each Unit may use a different point.
When attacking from an Area, Line of Sight and range are measured from the edge point that Squad is Sited at—this is always at Ground level.
Squads may not attack others inside the same Zone (that happens later in CQB).
Buildings cannot be entered via a face on which an enemy Squad is Sited. Areas cannot be entered from any point within 3” of a point where an enemy Squad is Sited.

All Units shown have Clear Line of Sight to the Purple Condor, and the Condor has Clear Line of sight to all Tusks, as Lines of Sight from and to Aircraft are not affected by Areas. The Condor only has Obscured Line of Sight to the Legionnaires as they Occupy a Zone.

runs.t: Legionnaires are Sited on a single face of a Building and can draw Line of Sight from anywhere on that face. They have Clear Line of Sight to the Tusk but have no Line of Sight to the Drones.
All Occupiers are Obscured and may only be targeted with Weapons while Sited. These Weapons target Squads, not individual Units.

When targeting Sited Squads inside Buildings, any window or door on the face that Squad has been Sited on, excluding its corners, may be used to measure range and Line of Sight to it (it doesn’t have to be the same point they attacked from).

When targeting Sited Squads inside Areas, the point where that Squad has been Sited must be used. As with all Zones, you can only target Squads inside Areas if they are Sited, but you can draw Line of Sight through up to 3” of the Area to the point where they are Sited.

Things which affect Units within a radius outside the Zone, such as Blast Weapons, Field Weapons, Units with the Shield special rule, or destroyed Aircraft, do not affect Occupiers directly, including Sited Units.
If a rule says it can affect Occupiers within its radius, they can be affected if the Zone is within this radius.

You may only measure a radius or distance from an Occupier to anything outside the Zone if it is Sited. Measure as if you were attacking. From a Building, you may measure from a different point to each Unit measured to. Units Occupying the same Zone are always within the radius or distance.
A CQB occurs once an Infantry Squad completes a full activation Occupying a Zone containing enemies—it must begin and end its activation inside—and in which a CQB has not occurred this Round.
Fighting in a CQB is not attacking. CQBs are resolved in these steps:

items.t: Each player combines the OF values of each of their Units in the Zone, giving them a total number of CQB dice. If a Unit is Sited or has half or fewer of its DP remaining, it contributes half its OF (it isn’t halved twice).
The player without the Initiative rolls their CQB dice—Contesting players hit on 4+, Controlling players on 3+. Criticals do not occur.
That player freely allocates their hits against the enemy Squads.
Their opponent attempts to block each of these hits using only their Squad’s DF value.
Each remaining hit inflicts 1DP on that Squad.
The player with the Initiative completes steps 2-5. Their CQB dice are not re-totalled.

If enemy Occupiers remain in the Zone, each Occupying Squad that has been damaged in this CQB and with half or fewer of its original Units remaining must take a Bravery test. You may elect to fail without rolling, even if the Squad has more than half of its Units remaining.

If the test is failed, the Squad must immediately exit the Zone or transfer into another Zone which touches it. This does not count towards any Unit’s Embark/Disembarks. The Squad may not exit directly into a Transport.
If this would result in all Squads exiting, one of the Controlling player’s Squads may remain if that player wishes. Otherwise, the Squad with the most Units left must remain (dice-off if tied).
If enemy Occupiers remain, the Zone’s Controlling player, if there is one, becomes a Contesting player.

runs.t: Features are distinct elements of a Zone with special rules. Scenarios will specify which to use. Features are represented by tokens or removable parts since they can be destroyed.
For every 5 damage a Zone takes during a single activation, the active player may remove one Feature from that Zone instead of inflicting 5DP. Collateral Damage is still inflicted.
Each Weapon in the following table corresponds to a Feature with the same name. A Zone may have duplicates of the same Weapon Feature.

In the Fire Weapon Features step of the Activation Phase, the player with the Initiative picks a Zone they Control with Weapons Features, activates it, and attacks with it like a Squad. Next, their opponent picks one of theirs, and so on until all Zones with Weapons Features have been activated.
Range and Line of Sight for each Weapon may together be measured from any point on a Building or any edge point on an Area.
A Zone gains the following rules if it has any of these Features—their effects are duplicated if it has multiple, identical Features:
ACM Package
— Weapons with two R values that target this Zone or its Occupiers must use their 2nd value.
Automated Sentries
— Each Infantry Squad entering this Zone takes 2D6 Small Arms hits before entering. Once a player Controls this Zone, only enemy Infantry are hit.
Comms Uplink
— This Zone’s Controller generates an additional CP in the Planning Phase.
Jamming Device
— Units within 8” of this Zone that are enemies of this Zone’s Controller gain UC and cannot benefit from Aegis.
Power Core

— If this Feature is destroyed, this Zone takes 3D6 damage. This damage may not be converted into destroying another Feature. If this Zone is destroyed by this or destroyed with this Feature, Units are potentially damaged within 4” rather than the usual 2”.
Seal
— This Zone can’t be entered through any of its faces or edges.
Shield Generator
— This Zone gains 4+ Passive countermeasures.
Shimmer Field

— Weapons can never hit this Zone or its Occupiers on a better roll than 4+ instead of always hitting it on a 2+. This cannot be modified, even by special rules. Weapons with an Ac value of A hit this Zone automatically.
These Features cannot be destroyed. Remove them if their Zone is destroyed.
Basement

— Squads may be Sited in the basement. Squads Sited in the basement cannot attack or be attacked, even by Weapons with Flame or Seeker. They have DF2+ against Collateral Damage hits and suffer -1 to Search rolls (see page 36 ‘Objects’).
Excellent Vantage
— When attacking from this Zone, Infantry Weapons gain +1E and +6” to their R value/s. Their Small Arms Weapons may attack aircraft within 12” rather than 9”.
Internal Flaw

— A Controlling player whose Squad begins its activation Occupying this Zone may instantly destroy it at the end of any friendly activation, providing none of their Squads still Occupy it. If their opponent becomes the Controller, the player loses this ability.
Secret Entrance
— This Feature comes in pairs, placed on one Zone and one point on the Table. Infantry may enter that Zone from this point. Squads cannot be Sited on that point.
Underground Monorail
—This Feature comes in pairs, placed on two Zones. Infantry may transfer between those Zones as if they were touching.

These are special Zones where only a small part is visible on the surface. These cannot be damaged or destroyed. Features placed on Bunker Entrances by Scenarios cannot therefore be destroyed, but they cannot gain Features during games. Only one Squad may be Sited on Bunker Entrances.

The Scenario will dictate where to place important Zones and other functional scenery. Scenarios do not usually define where to place non-critical scenery, but plenty should be used. As a guideline, a 48”x48” table should have 15-20 Zones of varying sizes. Other scenery choices are up to players.
Zones are interchangeable between Areas and Buildings unless the Scenario specifies which. All Zones have normal Armour unless the Scenario specifies which.

Territories are where each player’s Groups begin the game or enter the Table from. If the Territory includes a Table Edge/s, Groups enter from those Edges. If it does not, Groups enter from any point within it.
A player’s Table Edge ends at the edge of their Territory if it does not cover the whole side of the Table. A Territory may be just a Table Edge / a portion of one/s.
Games last 6 Rounds unless the Scenario says otherwise. If the available time runs out or a player’s Army is wiped out, the game ends early.

Vehicles and Infantry which do not begin the game aboard an Aircraft, or in a Transport aboard an Aircraft, always begin Reserved. Otherwise, Scenarios / special rules specify how your Groups may enter. Once on the Table, Units cannot normally leave it. Groups may enter in these ways:

These Groups begin on the Table within their Territory. Before the game’s first Initiation Phase, each player rolls a D6, and the lowest scoring places one of these Groups. Alternate until all these Groups are placed.
Infantry may Deploy inside a Zone which touches this Territory. Units may be Deployed outside of their Transports, but only within 3” of them.
These Groups begin off the Table and may enter when activated.
These Groups begin off the Table and become Ready from Round 2.
These Groups may only enter when and where a rule allows them to, often not from their Territory. Units in Holding at the end of the game count as destroyed.

Scenarios award players Victory Points (VP)—the player with the most wins. Ties are resolved by who has the most Kill Points (KP)—the total points cost of all enemy Units and Commanders they destroyed.
Players are awarded VP for meeting Scenario Objectives. Any points or KP requirements for Scenario Objectives are halved for Skirmish-sized games.
Some Scenarios award VP on certain Rounds—award these in those Round’s End Phases. Otherwise, VPs are awarded as Scenario Objectives are achieved.
Players are awarded X VP at the end of the game for every 200 KP they have scored.
Players are awarded X VP for Extracting certain Objects (see page 36 ‘Objects’). Otherwise, Y VP are awarded at the end of the game for Objects you Carry but have not Extracted.
Players gain X VP at the end of the game for every 200pts of Vehicles they have within regions indicated by the Scenario.

Players with 200pts or more of Vehicles within certain Table segments Challenge for Y VP per segment. Or, players with the most points of Vehicles within those segments, and only if they have 200pts or more there, Dominate for X VP per segment.
Since a Unit’s centre is infinitely small, it can’t be in two segments.
When a Squad completes a full activation Occupying certain Zones—it must begin and end its activation inside—its player gains X VP. Each Zone may only yield VP in this way once per player per game.
Players are awarded X VP for Controlling certain Zones, or Y VP for Contesting them. If the Zone is destroyed, players no longer score for that Zone.
Players are awarded X VP at the end of the game if certain Zones are not Compromised, or Y VP if they are not destroyed. Compromised Zones have half or fewer of their initial DP remaining.
Players are awarded X VP when certain Zones are destroyed, or Y VP if they are Compromised at the end of the game. Compromised Zones have half or fewer of their initial DP remaining.

Players are awarded VP for having Vehicles within 3” of certain Zones or within 6” of certain points. Players Secure the Zone/point for X VP if only they have Vehicles there, or Challenge instead for Y VP if they have 100pts or more of Vehicles there. If the Zone is destroyed, players no longer score for that Zone.
For the Extract Scenario Objective, the capture and/or extraction of movable Objects is the goal. Objects are represented by tokens—the Scenario will dictate where to place them.
Objects must be found before they can be interacted with.
Objects on Ground are found by moving over them with Infantry or a Vehicle.

Objects inside Zones must be Searched for. When an Occupying Squad begins its Activation, it may Search. Roll 1D6—on a 6+ for Large Zones or a 5+ for other sizes, the Object is found. If no enemy Units Occupy this Zone, Squads gain +1 to this roll. Squads which Searched this Zone in one or more previous Rounds gain +1 to this roll.
Each player may only Search a Zone up to twice per Round.
A Unit that finds an Object may carry it. If it was found inside a Zone, any Unit in the Squad that Searched may carry it.
Only Infantry and Vehicles, or Aircraft which can directly carry Infantry, may Transport Objects. Aircraft may transport Units carrying Objects.
Carrying an Object does not require Transport capacity. A Unit may carry multiple Objects.

children.heading: Passing, Dropping, and Picking up Objects

runs.t: Objects may be passed between friendly Units up to 2” apart during either Unit’s activation. A Unit inside a Zone which contains no enemies may pass it to a friendly Unit within 1” of an Entrance during either Unit’s activation. Objects may be passed between friendly Units inside Zones at any time, including the instant they are destroyed.
A Unit may drop an Object at any point during its activation—place it underneath that Unit where it is dropped or inside the Zone in which it was dropped.
A Unit may pick up an Object inside a Zone it’s Occupying during its activation, or by moving over it.
For Vehicles and Aircraft, picking up or being passed an Object counts as Embarking.
If a Unit carrying an Object outside a Zone is destroyed, that Object is destroyed on a 5+. Otherwise, place it where the carrying Unit was destroyed.
If a Unit carrying an Object inside a Zone is destroyed, and if there are no friendly Units to pass it to, then its player must either:

items.t: Drop it inside the Zone. If enemy Occupiers remain in the Zone, one of those Units of their player’s choice gains it.
Try to pass it to a friendly Unit within 1” of an Entrance. On a 5+, the player may pass it. Otherwise, it is dropped inside the Zone as above.

runs.t: If a Unit carrying an Object fails a Bravery Test at the end of a CQB and has no friendly Occupiers to pass it to, it must drop it inside the Zone. If enemy Occupiers remain after the CQB, one of those Units of their player’s choice gains it.

If a Building is destroyed containing an un-carried Object, that Object is destroyed on a 3+. Otherwise, it remains inside the replacement Area. If an Area is destroyed containing an un-carried Object, that Object is destroyed.
If a Zone is destroyed containing a carried Object, it is destroyed if the Unit carrying it is destroyed and it has no friendly (soon to be former) Occupiers to pass it to.
An Object that leaves the Table as specified below has been Extracted and is removed from the game:

items.t: Squads may leave the Table from any Table Edge within their Territory if carrying an Object, transporting a carrying Unit, or sharing a Transport with one—simply move them off the Table. They become Ready and may return next Round from the same Table Edge.
This works like Friendly Lines, but the Object must be Extracted from a Table Edge within the opponent’s Territory.
One or more points are specified for each player. Each Carried Object that player has within 3” of one of their points at the end of the game is Extracted.
