Friendly Units within X” of this Unit lose UC.
During CQBs, this Unit automatically passes X DF rolls—each Unit in the Squad contributes X. It cannot automatically pass First Strike hits but gains +1DF against them.
Agile Units gain +1DF against Collateral Damage hits.
Enemy Aircraft within X” of one or more Units with this rule may be attacked with a +1Ac bonus.
While Occupying a Zone containing enemies, Bloodthirsty Infantry suffer -2 to Search rolls and may not exit.
Breachers may enter a Building from any point on it—they do not require an Entrance. Breachers ignore Sited enemies and the Automated Sentries and Seal Effect Features when entering Zones.
When a Squad with Breachers enters a Building, select one random enemy Occupying Squad. Each Breaching Unit inflicts X Small Arms hits on that Squad.
This Unit may move over any scenery that isn’t Impassable Ground.
If this Unit contains a Commander, double the Radius of Command Cards measured from this Unit.
This Transport cannot Disembark or Embark Units in the same Round that it Disembarks.
If this Infantry Unit begins its activation inside a Zone, you may place a Demo Charge Token on that Zone. If enemy Occupiers are present, its Squad must pass a Bravery Test first.

If you have no Occupiers in a Zone containing your Demo Charge Tokens, you may remove them all at the end of any friendly activation—each inflicts 2DP on that Zone on an X+. This suffers -1 if one enemy Occupying Squad is present, or -2 if more than one is present.
Friendly Squads Occupying the same Zone as one or more friendly Dogs Units gain +1 to Search rolls.
During step 3 of CQBs, players must allocate at least 1 hit to each enemy Squad with Dogs per remaining DP that Squad has before allocating any to other Squads.
Dogs with Living Weapons may Embark into Transports.
Weapons attacking targets with Ev suffer -X Ac. Ev is ignored when targeting friendly Units.

Fast Movers are Aircraft with two Mv stats—a minimum and maximum. They must move at least their minimum Mv each activation, in a straight line, and before attacking. They may move less than their minimum Mv when entering the Table. They may pivot up to 45 degrees at the beginning of their move and again at its end. Units within a Fast Mover Squad must end their move parallel to each other, facing the same way.
Fast Movers can always move off the Table. If any Unit in the Squad moves off, the Squad leaves the Table. They then return to Ready.
Fast Movers ALWAYS begin the game Reserved.
Fast Movers are ignored for determining Victory Points but do concede Kill Points.
Commanders may not be assigned to Fast Movers.

A Fast Mover Squad can elect to fly high at the end of its move, before pivoting– indicate this with a token. High-fliers can pivot up to 180 degrees. High-fliers can only target and be targeted by other Fast Movers flying high. Nothing blocks Line of Sight to high-fliers.
A high-flier can end its move in illegitimate places, including over Zones - remove it from its flight stand/substitute a token for it if it can’t stand up.
The Squad remains flying high until it leaves the Table or elects to return to normal height. It may do this at the end of its move, before pivoting.
If this Unit does not Embark, Disembark, or attack in an activation, it gains +X” Mv.

At the start of a CQB, each non-Sited Unit with First Strike inflicts X Small Arms hits on the enemy Squads, distributed freely. If both players have First Strike Units involved, the player without the Initiative distributes their hits first. DF saves are then attempted simultaneously.

Instead of using its DF, even if it would not normally be able to, this Infantry Unit may use a save of X+ against hits from Weapons, Collateral Damage, and Command Cards. Hits from anything above E2 ignore this rule.
This Unit may always Deploy up to X” from their Territory. Infiltrating Infantry may Deploy as Occupiers in a Zone, but that Zone must be wholly within X” of their Territory.

Non-Auxiliary Transports of Squads with Infiltrate that choose to Infiltrate must begin Ready—they are allowed to start empty. Otherwise, Units cannot Infiltrate if part of a Group containing Units without Infiltrate.
A Transport with Infiltrate confers Infiltrate to all Units aboard.

If it does not Embark or Disembark from a Unit that activation, this Unit may Jump when it starts moving—during its move, but not at its end, it is an Aircraft with an X” Mv. If Embarking/Disembarking from a Zone, this Mv is not halved.
If an AA Weapon Reaction Attacks it, this Unit suffers -3A for that attack. Line of Sight is measured to a point 2” above the Jumper. Jump Infantry are still damaged as Infantry.
Large Vehicles cannot be Obscured except by Obscured Status Tokens granted by Stealth—otherwise, if Obscured, you have Clear Line of Sight.
If any part of a Large Vehicle miniature is within 2” of a Building when that Building is destroyed, it takes hits as if its centre was within 2”.

When attacking with a Large Vehicle’s Weapons, use the Weapon’s pivot point (if it’s on a ball joint or turret) or the base of the barrel (if it’s fixed) to determine range and Line of Sight for that Weapon. Arcs should be drawn from the centre of the model as usual.
When Embarking or Disembarking into or from a Large Transport, add 2” to the allowed Embark/Disembark distance.
If the size of a Large Vehicle makes it impossible for a Weapon to get into range against it, physical contact is sufficient.
CQB dice contributed by this Unit hit automatically.
Commanders cannot be assigned to Living Weapons. They may begin the game aboard a Transport but may not Embark into one. They may enter Zones.
Living Weapons cannot Search for or carry Objects. They cannot exit Zones with enemy Occupiers. A player with only Living Weapon Occupiers can only Contest that Zone.

Living Weapons with the same name Occupying the same Zone automatically form one Squad/ join an existing Squad of Living Weapons with the same name at the start of the Initiation Phase—their player may choose which Squad they join. This can take the Squad above its maximum Squad size.
All friendly Vehicle and Infantry Units within X” of this Unit are Obscured to enemies.
This Unit may attempt to block any damage it would receive by rolling 1 D6 for each point of damage—each result of at least X blocks the damage.
Against damage from E9 sources, after modifiers are applied, Passive Countermeasures suffer a -1 modifier. E10 sources, after modifiers are applied, ignore Passive Countermeasures.
Once all modifiers are applied, Passive Countermeasures can never exceed 3+.
Occupiers inside Zones with Passive Countermeasures gain those Passive Countermeasures against damage dealt directly by Weapons.

An Aircraft transporting Rapid Insertion Units which have not Embarked this Round may move up to an additional X” after all other modifiers are applied before these Units Disembark. The Aircraft cannot move further than its unmodified Mv using this rule.
Units with Rapid Insertion may Disembark when their Transport is within 3” of an enemy Vehicle.
This Unit recovers X lost DP in the Cleanup step of the End Phase.
Criticals from non-Blast Weapon hits below E9, after modifiers are applied, do not inflict any additional damage against this Unit.

This Unit gains Clear Line of Sight against targets that would otherwise be Obscured. Other Units in this Unit’s Squad, and other Units in its Group within 4”, also gain Clear Line of Sight against targets that would otherwise be Obscured.
You may measure a Command Card’s Radius from friendly Scout Units.
If a Weapon with Indirect draws Line of Sight from this Unit, the -2Ac penalty is ignored.
All Units/Zones as defined by X within Y” of this Unit gain Z+ Passive Countermeasures.
Skimmers ignore all types of Ground and may move over protruding Ground details less than 1” high. Skimmers may drop down any incline.

If it will spend its full activation disembarked, this Squad may choose to only move OR move 0” and attack. If it does, this Squad gains an Obscured Status Token. Squads with Obscured Status Tokens are Obscured.
This Unit may always begin the game Ready. Units Disembarking directly from this Unit gain Assault on their Weapons.

Per Squad with two or more Strong Units in a CQB, one enemy Squad of your choosing suffers -1DF for that CQB, assigned at the start of step 1 of that CQB. If both players have Strong Units involved, the player without the Initiative chooses an enemy Squad(s) to affect first.

If one or more friendly Units with Surveyor are within 1” of a Zone with friendly Occupiers at the end of the Round, you may place one Mapping Token on that Zone. When Searching for an Objective, you may spend two Mapping Tokens on that Zone to find the Objective on a 2+.
If you have no friendly Units with Surveyor within 1” of a Zone at the end of any activation (yours or your opponent’s), remove all your Mapping Tokens from it.
Enemies Occupying the same Zone as Terror Units suffer -1B and -1 to Search rolls.
If a Weapon targeting this Unit has two R values, it may always use its first.
Units in this Squad must maintain a coherency of X” rather than the usual 3”.
Only AA Weapons can target Aircraft normally. AA Weapons ignore Ev on non-Aircraft. AA Weapons may Reaction Attack—see main rules.
This AA Weapon may only Reaction Attack but suffers no penalty for doing so.
This AA Weapon may not Reaction Attack.
Units may only attack with one Weapon with the same ALT number (X) each Round.
Line of Sight may be measured from a point 1” above the model’s centre when attacking with this Weapon.

This Weapon may attack on the same round as Disembarking from a Transport, and/or entering or exiting a Zone. If it does any of these it suffers -2 Ac, or -1 Ac if it has a R of CC. It still may not attack in the same Round as Embarking into a Transport.
If a Unit with an Assault Weapon Disembarks then moves 0”, it counts as having moved 1” for attacking purposes.

This Weapon gains X E for each other instance of this Weapon in coherency. Only one Battery Weapon with the same name may attack per Squad per Round. If one attacks, each other instance of that Weapon in coherency counts as having attacked.

This Weapon uses the Blast Template — a 5” diameter circle. First, place the template’s centre over the target’s centre—this is the primary target. Place all templates from one activation’s attacks simultaneously. All Units and Zones within the template are now targets. Roll to hit once against each target for each template. If the primary target was Obscured, everything under the template is Obscured, otherwise Obscured is ignored. Roll D6 times per template against Infantry.
If the primary target is a Vehicle with Large or a Zone, do not place the template but roll to hit D3 times. This Weapon can inflict Critical damage against Zones.
If the primary target is a Sited Squad, do not place the template. Instead, roll to hit the Squad D6 times. Roll to hit the Zone once.
If the primary target is an Aircraft, only Aircraft under the template and not flying high are targets. If the primary target is a non-Aircraft, aircraft are not targets.
If a Unit is hit by this Weapon, place a Concussed Status Token on its Squad. Concussed Squads suffer -2Ac. Concussed Infantry also count as Sited in CQBs and do not contribute to Entrances Covered.
This Weapon inflicts X additional DP for each Critical it inflicts against Units.
This Weapon can inflict Critical damage against Zones. It also inflicts X additional DP for each success when rolling to inflict damage against Zones.

If this Weapon hits by rolling equal to or higher than X, it will automatically cause a Critical instead of rolling to damage. This counts as a successful roll to damage. This Weapon’s Ac cannot be modified below X.
This Weapon inflicts X additional DP for each success when rolling to inflict damage against Units.
This Weapon may suffer -X E to double its R value/s. It may do this twice to quadruple its R.
This Weapon may measure range and Line of Sight from any point its Unit moved through that activation if it moved in a single straight line. It may pivot before moving.

This Weapon does not target anything. Instead, each Zone, Vehicle, and Infantry Unit within its R are assigned attacks equal to its Att. Since it does not target anything, Line of Sight is not needed and friendlies may be hit.
Units within this Weapon’s Squad are not damaged by it and cannot receive Concussed, Jammed, or Suppressed Status Tokens from it.
If this Weapon has AA, its attacks are assigned to Aircraft instead of Zones, Vehicles, and Infantry.
If this Weapon places Status Tokens, place one on every Squad within its R that could receive the Token. This counts as placing one of that Token.
This Weapon’s Ac and R values cannot be modified.
This Weapon ignores the Ac penalty against Obscured targets, and it ignores Evasion. Infantry suffer -1DF against this Weapon.
This Weapon may target Occupiers as if they were Sited anywhere on a Zone.
If friendly Squads are present in this Zone, all misses from your Flame Weapons which targeted enemies in this Zone this activation hit one random friendly Squad in that Zone instead.
Flame Weapons with Small Arms may also combine their attacks against Zones. This Weapon can inflict Critical damage against Zones. Flame Weapons gain +1 Demo against Areas.

You may discard any number of successful hits from one or more instances of this Weapon to add X E to another remaining hit. For example, two identical E2 Cannons with Focus 1 and 4 attacks each score a total of 6 hits. Their player chooses to discard 4 of these hits to add 2 Energy to each of the remaining hits, resulting in two E4 hits.
A Weapon with a R value of GB is a Gravity Bomb. It may target anything within 2” of any point its Unit moved over that Round. Line of Sight is checked from that point.
This Weapon ignores the Ac penalty for Obscured targets. Sited Infantry may not use their DF value to block hits from this Weapon.

Each hit from this Weapon that inflicts 1 or more damage against a Building inflicts X additional Collateral Damage hits. Each hit that inflicts 1 or more damage against an Area inflicts 2x X additional Collateral Damage hits.
When attacking with this Weapon, any other friendly Unit may also be used to draw Line of Sight from, in which case it suffers -2Ac. If that friendly Unit has Scout, the -2Ac is ignored.
For Sited Units with Indirect, no portion of a Building they Occupy can lie between the face they are Sited on and their target.
This Weapon cannot damage or affect things of the type X.

If a Unit is hit by this Weapon, place a Jammed Status Token on its Squad. Weapons with two R values that attack a Jammed Squad may use their 1st value. Jammed Squads, and Units and Weapons within them, cannot be affected by their player’s Command Cards that take effect while the Squad is Jammed.
This Weapon may only attack X times/game.
This Weapon’s target must be in Clear or Obscured Line of Sight of a friendly Unit with Scout, or it suffers -2Ac.
If its Unit moves 0” (before or after attacking), this Weapon gains +X E that activation.
This Weapon may Reaction Attack against Vehicles and suffers no penalty for doing so. It may only Reaction Attack.

When rolling to inflict damage against Units, this Weapon may always succeed on a roll of X+ regardless of E or A values. This cannot be modified. This can alter the roll required for a Critical—Pen 4+ would inflict a Critical on a 6+.
If its Unit moves 0” (before or after attacking), this Weapon gains +X Ac that activation and if it has Destroyer, it also gains +X Destroyer.
This Weapon may only target Y, and Y may be a friendly Unit. For each hit by this Weapon, the target regains X lost DP.
This Weapon may target Occupiers as if they were Sited anywhere on a Zone. This Weapon ignores the Ac penalty against Obscured targets if they Occupy the same Zone as friendly Occupiers.
This uses the same rules as a Field Weapon, except that the attacking Unit is destroyed, and Units within its Squad can be damaged by it.
If a Unit with a Self-Destruct Weapon is destroyed while not Embarked, roll a D6. On a 4+, the Unit must immediately attack with the Weapon before being removed, even if it could not normally attack.

If a Squad receives at least as many hits from Weapons with Smoke during a single activation as it has Units, place an Obscured Status Token on that Squad. Squads with Obscured Status Tokens are Obscured.
This Weapon may target friendly Units and may target its own Unit.
When attacking during its Unit’s activation, this Weapon may freely split its attacks between Units within 3” of at least one other Unit it targets. This must be a single chain of targets.
If a Unit is hit by this Weapon, place a Suppressed Status Token on its Squad. Suppressed Squads may only move 0” if any Unit within it attacks. Suppressed Fast Movers may not attack.
This Weapon reduces the target’s Ev by X to a minimum of 0. For example, T2 would reduce Ev3 to Ev1.

Behemoths have a Groups Equivalent stat instead of Squad Size. A Behemoth counts as that many Groups when building your Army and generating Pass tokens but counts as 1 Group for the ‘no Group may cost more than 1/4 of your total allowed pts’ rule. Commanders cannot be assigned to Behemoths. Behemoths have the special Type ‘Behemoth’. They are treated as Vehicles with Large unless another rule contradicts this.
In casual games, players may agree to waive any of the Army building restrictions. Also, several special Behemoth Scenarios allow players to take Behemoths in your Army in other ways

Behemoths are so huge that several things cannot affect them: 1. Command Cards cannot target Behemoths. Cards which target ‘all’ of anything which include a Behemoth (e.g. all friendly Units) do not affect the Behemoth directly. 2. Command Abilities cannot target Behemoths. 3. Behemoths cannot receive Status tokens. 4. Behemoths cannot be Obscured, even by special rules. 5. Behemoths cannot carry Objects. 6. Friendly Shield and Repair special rules cannot affect Behemoths. 7. Passive Countermeasures on Behemoths are unmodified by E9 and E10 sources. 8. Criticals on Behemoths with Resilient do not inflict any additional damage, regardless of the Energy of the Weapon.

Behemoths activate differently from normal Groups, and often multiple times per Round. What is possible is governed by their Power stat. Behemoths begin each Round with a number of Power tokens (PT) equal to their Power. When you may activate a normal Group, you may instead activate a Behemoth with PT remaining. It must then complete one Action from the Power Table:
Reposition (PT Cost 1): Move up to half Mv
Advance (PT Cost 3): Move up to full Mv
Fire (PT Cost 1): Attack with 1 Weapon
Volley (PT Cost 3): Attack with 2 Weapons
Charge (PT Cost 2): Add 1 to this Behemoth's Power next Round
Discharge (PT Cost 1): None
Use Gear (PT Cost Varies): Use one Gear. See ‘Gear’

You may move each Behemoth up to twice per Round, up to its full Mv each time. Normal Mv limits for Embarking/Disembarking are ignored for Behemoths, but they may only Embark/Disembark Units on Reposition. You may use each Gear once per Round. Each Weapon may attack once per Round. Normal MA limits apply—the total distance from both allowed moves is used.
Unless a Scenario specifies an entry requirement for Behemoths, players have two options. Players must simultaneously reveal which they will be using for each Behemoth before the game begins.
This Behemoth begins Reserved and must enter using an Advance Action.

This Behemoth begins in Holding and may only enter via Drop Harness from Round 2. At the end of its activation, a friendly Unit that has not Embarked/Disembarked this Round and has Scout, Command Centre, or contains a Commander may designate a point within 12” of itself in Line of Sight. That point must be on open Ground and at least 3” from any Unit or Zone. Next, move that point D6-2” in a random direction. Place that Behemoth with its centre on that point (see ‘Moving and Placing Behemoths’). This counts as a move for the Behemoth and it has 2PT remaining that Round.

Behemoths ignore Exceptional and Poor Ground. Impassable Ground only applies for the Behemoth’s centre. Follow the usual rules for moving over protruding details. Most won’t hamper a Behemoth and should be ignored when placing one unless reasonable judgement says otherwise. Players may need to temporarily remove protruding details when placing Behemoths.

Behemoths may move through and end their move overlapping Areas. Behemoths must use 2” of their available Mv for every 1” of Area their centre crosses. If any part of a Behemoth, but not its centre, moved through or overlaps an Area, that Area takes D3 damage and the Behemoth takes D3-2 E9 hits—use the same dice result for both. If a Behemoth’s centre moved through or overlaps an Area, that Area takes D6 damage and the Behemoth takes D6-4 E9 hits—use the same dice result for both. If necessary, substitute a 3D Area for a 2D one when placing Behemoths.

Behemoths may move through Buildings but may not end their move overlapping them. If a rule would force one to overlap with a Building, the Behemoth’s player must shift it so that they are in contact but not overlapping if there’s no alternative. Behemoths must use 3” of their available Mv for every 1” of Building their centre crosses. For Behemoths with a starting DP of 10 or fewer, their centres may not move through a Building. If any part of a Behemoth, but not its centre, moved through a Building, that Building takes D6 damage and the Behemoth takes D6-3 E9 hits—use the same dice result for both. If a Behemoth’s centre moved through a Building, or if any part of it was forced to overlap with one, roll 1D6 for each of that Building’s starting DP. Each 4+ inflicts 1 damage on that Building. Each 6 also inflicts an E9 hit on that Behemoth.

Behemoths may move through non-Behemoth Units. Each enemy Vehicle or Infantry Unit moved through takes D3-1 damage. Each time a 3 is rolled for a Vehicle with 3 or more starting DP, that Behemoth takes an E9 hit. Behemoths may end their move overlapping non-Behemoth Units. Aircraft must then be shifted the minimum possible distance by their player, maintaining coherency. Vehicles and Infantry are destroyed. For each Vehicle destroyed, roll 1D6 for each of its starting DP. Each 4+ inflicts an E9 hit on that Behemoth.
Areas are ignored when drawing Line of Sight to/from Behemoths. Otherwise, attacking Behemoths involves these additional rules:
Weapon attacks of E5 or higher gain Focus 2 against Behemoths.

Behemoths suffer -1A if attacked by Weapons within the Behemoth’s rear arc. Use the same arcs the Behemoth would use to attack to determine if it is being targeted in the rear. Behemoths suffer -1A if attacked by non-CC Weapons within 6”. Both may apply for -2A.
Weapons always hit Behemoths on a 2+. This cannot be modified, even by special rules, except by aiming for Systems Damage and Decoys. Weapons with an Ac value of A hit Behemoths automatically.

These Weapon Special rules suffer modifiers against Behemoths: 1. Destroyer Weapons on non-Behemoths suffer -1 Destroyer. 2. Pen Weapons of E3 or lower suffer -1Pen after all other modifiers are applied. If applied to Pen 6+, Pen is ignored. 3. Grav Weapons gain only +5E and +1 Devastator against Behemoths.

Behemoths have multiple DP values (e.g. 7,14, 20). The final value its actual DP. If it has not been damaged up to the first value, it is Intact. For Behemoths with 2 values, if it has been damaged up to the first value or higher, it is Crippled. For Behemoths with 3 values, if it has been damaged up to the first value or higher, it is Degraded. If it has been damaged up to the second value or higher, it is Crippled. Degraded Behemoths cannot use Advance. Crippled Behemoths cannot use Advance or Charge. They are worth half their pts for scenario and scoring purposes, including KP.

If an enemy Behemoth begins a friendly activation Intact, you may roll one D3 against the Systems Damage Table at the end of that activation for every 3 damage it takes directly from non-CC Weapon attacks during that activation. Roll for each 3 damage and apply the effect before rolling again (e.g. if 6 damage was dealt). If it was Degraded at the beginning of that activation, roll 2D3 instead. If it was Crippled at the beginning of that activation, roll 3D3 instead.
ACM Offline (Result 0-1): Weapons may use their 1st R value against this this Round.
Power Fluctuations (Result 2): -1 PT. Cannot use Advance or Charge next Round.
Drive Destabilised (Result 3): Cannot move again this Round. Can only move once next Round.
Gear Destroyed (Result 4): Cannot use one random Gear (permanent).
Drive Damaged (Result 5): Reposition and Advance cost +1PT (permanent).
Cell Destroyed (Result 6): -1 PT. Suffers -1 Power (permanent).
Optics Damaged (Result 7): All Weapons suffer -1Ac. Cannot aim for Systems Damage (permanent).
Internal Explosion (Result 8): Takes D3 damage.
Weapon Destroyed (Result 9): One random non-Secondary Weapon* cannot attack (permanent).
Armour Cracked (Result 10): Suffers -1A (permanent).
Core Rupture (Result 11): Remove all PT. Suffers -2PT and -1A (permanent).
Heart Shot (Result 12): Behemoth destroyed.

For results 4 and 9, if an already destroyed System/Weapon is chosen, apply results 5 and 8 instead, respectively. Otherwise, duplicate results are cumulative. * For this roll, Weapons with the same Alt value count as a single Weapon.

Immediately before declaring targets when attacking, you may declare you are aiming for Systems Damage against one or more enemy Behemoths. For that activation, your non-CC Weapons suffer -1 to the roll required to hit that Behemoth. For that activation, you may modify any Systems Damage result against it by up to three, and you choose which System/Weapon is destroyed for results 4 and 9.

When a Behemoth is destroyed, it is not immediately removed. Instead, its player must roll 1D6 against the Mortal Damage table at the end of the current activation and apply the result before removing it. Add 1 to the result if that Behemoth had a starting DP of 15 or higher:
Slumped (Result 1-2): Leave the miniature in place. It is still destroyed.
Blaze of Glory (Result 3): That Behemoth may make a Fire or Volley Action if it has sufficient PT. Then, apply result 4.
Cell Burst (Result 4): Units and Zones within 6" suffer an E6 hit. Place a Jammed Status Token on every Squad this damages.
Structural Collapse (Result 5): Non-Behemoth Vehicles and Infantry within D3+4" are destroyed on a 5+ (roll for each). Behemoths and Zones within 6" take D6 E10 hits.

Magazine Detonation (Result 6): Within 2D6", Units suffer an E10 hit, Infantry and Units with 1 starting DP are destroyed, and Zones suffer D6 damage. Place a Concussed Status Token on every Squad this damages.
Core Implosion (Result 7): Units and Zones within D3+5" are destroyed.

Some Behemoths are Transports. Except for Behemoths with the Director Gear, Behemoths taken with Squads aboard do not share a Group with their transported Squads. Instead, all Squads aboard a Behemoth at the start of the game form a single Group. They may Disembark during their own Activation or while their Behemoth makes a Reposition Action. A Behemoth’s Mv is not reduced if it Disembarks Units, but no Units may Disembark from a Behemoth during a Round in which it makes an Advance action. Units cannot Embark into Transport Behemoths other than Gate Behemoths. Any Units Embarked in a Behemoth when it is destroyed are destroyed.
Behemoths often incorporate non-Weapon equipment that expends PT to use (cost shown before each System’s name on the Behemoth’s stat sheet). These are:

This Behemoth has a Transport capacity specifically for Squads with Directed. X states the number of those Squads and Y states the number of Units within them. The Behemoth is their Director, and they are Directed by it. A Behemoth with Director begins the game with its Transport capacity filled. When this Behemoth uses this Gear, it may Disembark one Squad of Directed Units. Directed Units are a part of this Behemoth’s Group but can only activate when it uses this Gear, at the end of that Action. Directed Units are destroyed when their Behemoth is destroyed. Otherwise, they act as normal Units.

When it next moves, this Behemoth’s Mv becomes X” and it ignores all scenery and Units while moving. Placing it, though, follows the normal rules. Its next move Action costs 0PT (either Reposition or Advance).
Enemy Weapons suffer -1 to the roll required to hit this Behemoth this Round. This System may only be used once per game and is ignored for Gear Destroyed results once used.

This Gear cannot be used in a Use Gear Action. Instead, immediately before rolling Passive Countermeasure saves due to enemy attacks, you may spend any amount of PT. If you do, you may have two of the saves per PT spent negate the incoming damage on a 2+, after all other modifiers are applied. You may do this any number of times per Round. If you roll a 1 for any of these upgraded saves, this Gear is destroyed at the end of that enemy activation. If this Gear is destroyed, this Behemoth loses its Passive Countermeasures.

Remove one permanent Effect from Systems Damage on this Behemoth. Weapon Destroyed requires double this System’s PT cost to remove. This cannot be used to remove Weapon Destroyed from Integral Weapons. This System may only be used once per game and is ignored for Gear Destroyed results once used.
This Behemoth recovers X lost DP.
One Behemoth in Line of Sight suffers an additional -1 Ac penalty when Aiming for Systems Damage this Round. In addition, that Behemoth must spend +X PT to Use Gear this Round.
On an X+, you opponent cannot aim for Systems Damage against this Behemoth until the start of its first Action next Round.

Pick an enemy Squad in Clear Line of Sight of this Behemoth. Weapons fired by this Behemoth in later Actions this Round gain +3Ac against that Squad and may ignore the accuracy reduction incurred by aiming for Systems Damage.
Weapons with Capacitors on this Behemoth gain the stated effect when attacking this Round.

This Unit may not be taken in your Army—it is included with its Behemoth. This Unit cannot activate or Embark/Disembark except when its Behemoth’s Director Gear is used. It does not count towards your Groups when generating pass tokens. It cannot carry Objects. If this Unit’s Behemoth is destroyed, this Unit is destroyed.

This Behemoth functions as an Auxiliary Gate, except that Squads can only Embark/ Disembark from it outside of its activation. In addition, this Behemoth may attack in the same Round as Embarking/Disembarking Units. A Gate Behemoth’s movement is not reduced if Units Embark into or Disembark from it, but no Units may Embark or Disembark from this Behemoth during a Round in which it makes an Advance action.
This Behemoth’s centre counts as any other part of it when moving over or being placed on Zones.

Many Behemoths stride into battle and can move dynamically. On something this huge, its pose could excessively advantage/disadvantage it. Treat Walkers as if they were a solid cylinder with an X” radius and Y” high. When measuring to/from a Walker, use any point within this cylinder to determine range and Line of Sight (use the same point for both). Arcs should be drawn to/from the centre of the model as usual. Walkers must still conform to the normal placement rules too—parts of the model that protrude from this cylinder still count, but ONLY when placing. Be mindful of this when building them. An ultra-wide pose might make one needlessly awkward to place.
This Weapon can gain one or more modifiers from a Weapons Capacitors System.

If this Weapon damages a Behemoth, you may make one D3 roll against that Behemoth on the Systems Damage table at the end of that activation. The result cannot be modified. Damage dealt by this Weapon still contributes to normal Systems Damage amounts, and this roll is in addition to any others.
If this Weapon damages a Behemoth, you may modify any Systems Damage roll against that Behemoth that activation by up to X.
This is a Blast Weapon but instead uses an 8” diameter template.

This Weapon can receive 2 Weapon Destroyed results from Systems Damage, and it requires 2 results before it cannot attack. It suffers -1E after one Weapon Destroyed result. This Weapon counts as 2 Weapons on the Actions table so can only attack using Volley.
This Weapon cannot attack non-Behemoth Units within X”.
Weapons with the same Linked number count as one Weapon for Actions and spending PT.

Macro Weapons have Strafe and may always use their 1st R value against non-Behemoths. They ignore Passive Countermeasures on non-Behemoths. Macro Weapons suffer -1Ac against Units with 2 or fewer starting DP. Against non-Behemoth Units, each hit inflicts 2DP without rolling to inflict damage. Since you do not roll to inflict damage, Criticals are not inflicted. However, if this Weapon has Devastator, it’s additional damage is still added—the automatic 2DP counts as one success. Infantry Units hit by Macro Weapons are destroyed. If hits would be assigned to the Squad instead of individual Units, one Unit in the Squad is destroyed per hit, starting with the most damaged. Damage dealt by Macro Weapons with CC does contribute to Systems Damage, but they do suffer the accuracy penalty when aiming for Systems Damage. If a Macro Weapon damaged a Behemoth on the same activation as it was destroyed, add 1 to the Mortal Damage result.
This Weapon may attack at the end of any of its Behemoth’s Actions in addition to other Weapons that attacked that Action.

Behemoths are still affected by this as the target is the opponent. If the roll in ‘Effect’ is failed when choosing to make an Action with a Behemoth, another Group must be chosen if any remain available.
This Unit may hold up to X RM Tokens (see other Bioficer special rules).

Bioficer Units with a hollow green square Transport Symbol (e.g. ) are Genitor Units. Genitor Units may begin the game with up to X Raw Materials (RM) tokens aboard them, and they may begin empty—X is shown within their Transport Symbol. When building your Army, RM tokens cost 5pts each and are assigned to those Genitor Units. Their points contribute to their Group’s total cost but do not contribute towards any category. In game, RM tokens are worth 0pts, so they do not contribute to KPs etc. Genitor Units may never have more than X RM tokens aboard—any above X are discarded. Genitor Units may not spend more than X RM tokens per activation (see Generated). RM Tokens may be passed between Genitor and Collector Units within 5” of each other during either Unit’s activation. Genitor Units cannot pass RM Tokens to Collectors. When Genitor Units could normally Disembark a Squad, they may Spawn a Squad of Generated Units. This new Squad must be within its Squad size limits. It Disembarks in the usual way and joins the Genitor Unit’s Group. Genitor Units may Spawn multiple Squads per Round. A Genitor Unit inside a Zone may Spawn Squads at the beginning of its activation. A Genitor Unit may not Spawn a Squad in the same Round as Embarking any Units.

Units of the category Generated are Generated Units. These have a solid green square Transport Symbol with thier RM cost X shown within it (e.g. ). These cannot be taken when building your Army. Generated Units may be Spawned by Genitor Units during the game. A Generated Unit costs X RM tokens to Spawn—remove those from the Genitor Unit as they Disembark. This is done by Unit—two Genitors with 3RM tokens each could not Spawn a Unit which costs 6RM.

Any number of Generated Squads, even if they are Living Weapons, may Embark into any Genitor Unit/s and may do so in either’s activation. Embark/Disembark limits are ignored for this. When a Squad does, remove it from the game and place X RM tokens for each Embarking Unit aboard those Genitor Unit/s, or half X for Units with half or fewer of their DP remaining. Any Objects a Unit was carrying are passed to that Genitor Unit, even if it’s an Aircraft. Generated Units are worth 5pts multiplied by X in game—shown with a red icon with thier points cost on their stats sheet.

Generated Units with a gold border on their Transport Symbol (e.g. ) may only be Spawned by a Genitor Unit with a gold number in its Transport Symbol. Advanced Genitors may Spawn non-advanced Generated Units. Advanced Generated Units may Embark into any Genitor as normal.
Grubs Occupying the same Zone as one or more Units with this rule gain +1OF and +1DF.

If this Unit it not within control range of a friendly Puppeteer, its OF becomes 1, its DF becomes 6+, it’s Mv becomes 0”, and it may not attack—these cannot be modified. Any special rules it has, besides Living Weapons, UC, and Puppet, cease to take effect. A player with only Puppet Occupiers out of control range may only Contest that Zone. You may not intentionally move Puppet Units out of control range.
This Unit controls friendly Puppet Units within X” of it, including Occupiers, and Occupiers in the same Zone. Any non-Infantry Unit containing a Bioficer Commander gains Puppeteer 9”.

Whenever an enemy Unit is destroyed in the same activation as being hit by a friendly Decon Weapon, you may place RM Tokens on 1 Genitor or Collector Unit within 15” of that Unit. If it had 1-2 initial DP, or was an Infantry Unit, place 2 tokens. Otherwise, place 4 tokens. At the end of step 8 of a CQB, if any of your involved Units had Decon Weapons at the start of this CQB, place 2 RM tokens per enemy Infantry Unit destroyed. You cannot do this more times than you had involved Units with Decon Weapons (e.g. if you had 2 Units with Decon Weapons involved, and 3 enemy Units were destroyed, you may place up to 4 tokens).
This Weapon has the Indirect and Ineffective: Zones special rules. It cannot target Aircraft and cannot attack while Sited.
At the start of this Unit’s activation, you may declare it will Supercruise. If you do, all its Weapons and any enemy Weapons targeting it suffer -1Ac until the end of the Round.

When outside a Zone, this Infantry Unit is treated as a Vehicle with an A value of X, although Blast Weapons still inflict D6 hits against them. In addition, Bikes have Resilient and are not affected by Devastator, and are still treated as Infantry for RM tokens placed by enemy Decon weapons (see Bioficer Weapon Special Rules). Small Arms Weapons always treat units with Bikes as Infantry, meaning they cannot combine attacks and inflict 1 DP per hit. Bikes units outside Zones may always roll their DF against Small Arms hits, even if not Obscured. They may still enter Zones. Bikes lose any Ev and Weapons while Occupying.

If an Infantry Unit will not Embark/Disembark from this Transport in its activation, this Transport gains that Infantry Unit’s Weapons that activation, except those with a R of CC. Those Weapons’ MA become Full and they lose Assault. This is cumulative with multiple Infantry Units. Those Weapons suffer -1Ac if this Transport Disembarks or moves over 0” that activation.
This Transport may be taken if at least half full.

You may only attack with this Weapon after moving and if its Unit may use its full move. If you attack with it, its Unit counts as moving its full Mv. Directly after the attack, this Weapon’s Unit loses 1DP on a 4+.

If your Army contains Subterranean Units, any of your Groups may start the game in Holding. The entire Group, including its transports, must be able to disembark from the Subterranean Units in your army, or be embarked in Transports capable of doing so. Unarmed Subterranean Units do not count against your number of allowed Groups. Subterranean Units with a Transport Symbol are not taken with any Units aboard. When a Subterranean Squad enters from Ready, it may be placed on Good or Exceptional Ground anywhere on the Table. If it is unarmed, it cannot activate from then on. Squads in Holding may Disembark from ANY Subterranean Unit(s) providing their Transport Symbols match. Squads which Embark into Subterranean Units are placed into Holding. Any Objects carried by Units Embarking into it leave the Table. Any Units which Embark cannot re-enter the Table that Round or next Round. Squads may Embark or Disembark into or from a Subterranean Unit outside of that Subterranean Unit’s activation. All other Embarking/Disembarking rules and restrictions still apply. Additionally, Subterranean Units may not Embark/ Disembark more than their Symbol indicates per Round, but they may do both. For example, one with could Embark , then Disembark . Units in Holding at the end of the game only count as destroyed if you have no Units which could return them to the Table if there were another Round.
Only Vehicles with an initial DP of 1, and Infantry, can Embark or Disembark into or from this Unit.
Only Vehicles with an initial DP of 1-2, and Infantry, can Embark or Disembark into or from this Unit.

One Squad with Cling may be chosen Embarked aboard any Aircraft without the Cling special rule, including non-Transports, with the same or more initial DP than this Squad’s combined DP—Transport Symbols are ignored. This Squad joins that Aircraft’s Group. Once Disembarked, it may not Embark into Transports.
Friendly Weapons with ‘plasma’ in their name gain +1E if they attack while within X” of this Unit. This is not cumulative with other Plasma Generators. Weapons on Fast Movers are not affected.

This Weapon may only target Zones. For each DP it inflicts, place 1 Unit of Razorworms in that Zone. All Razorworms placed in a Zone by Razorworm Pods form one Squad at the end of their Group’s attacks, within that Group. These Razorworms count as having Embarked into that Zone and may do nothing further that Round except fight in a CQB. Razorworms created via Razorworm Pods do not grant KP or otherwise count for Scoring, but do Contest or Control Zones as normal.
Spark Weapons gain Ac 2+ against Aircraft but cannot damage Zones.

If your Army contains Gates, any of your Squads may start the game in Holding. Gates are always Transports but are not taken with any Units aboard. Gates do not count against your number of allowed Groups. For Direct Deployment, each Gate is treated as a Group. A Gate is never part of another Group, but any number of them which have not yet been activated that Round may be activated together with any non-Gate Group. They then complete that activation as if they were a Group. Gates can only be activated this way except during in the Orphaned Transport Activations step of the Activation Phase, where any un-activated Gates must activate together. Squads in Holding may Disembark from ANY Gate/s providing their Transport Symbols match. Squads which Embark into Gates are placed into Holding. Any Objects they are carrying are passed to the Gate, even if it’s an Aircraft. Squads may Embark or Disembark into or from a Gate during their own Activation, even if the Gate is not a part of that Activation. All other Embarking/Disembarking rules and restrictions still apply. Additionally, Gates may not Embark/Disembark more than their Symbol indicates per Round, but they may do both. For example, a Gate with could Embark , then Disembark . Units in Holding at the end of the game only count as destroyed if you have no Units which could return them to the Table if there were another Round.

These are always Auxiliary Transports. They use the same rules as Gates except they are taken as non-Gate Squads and must be activated normally—they cannot be activated together with another non-Gate Group. Other Squads can still Embark/Disembark from them outside of that Aux Gate’s activation. Aux Gates cannot attack in the same round as Embarking/Disembarking. Command Cards which target Gates cannot target these.
Two or more non-Gate, non-Aircraft Squads within a Shaltari Army may form Groups if their combined points cost does not exceed 250pts.
This Weapon uses the same rules as an AA-R Weapon. Additionally, a Unit may only be targeted by a Weapon with this rule once during its activation.

When targeting Vehicles, add the target’s initial DP to this Weapon’s E. For Vehicles of A4 or higher add 1 more, or for Vehicles of A7 or higher add 2 more. For Vehicles with Large, it gains +1 Devastator. This Weapon ignores Resilient on Vehicles. This Weapon always damages Zones on a 3+ and has a Demo value equal to its E.
This Weapon ignores Passive Countermeasures and Resilient.

If a friendly Squad with Skimmer receives at least as many hits from Weapons with Skimcharger during a single Activation as it has Units, place a Skimcharged Status Token on its Squad. Skimcharged Squads gain Flat Out 5”, +5” MA on their Weapons, and may benefit from Flat Out even if they Attack (but not if they Embark or Disembark).

This Unit, and Units in coherency with it, gain Regenerate 2. At the beginning of this Unit’s activation, if all Units in its Squad are in coherency, you may place its Squad into Holding—this is an Embark operation. Any Objects this Squad is carrying must be dropped or passed to another Unit first.

Subservient Units gain +2B and +2OF when occupying a Zone containing a friendly Unit without Subservient. Subservient Units in a Squad which also contains Units without Subservient gain any special rules those Units have. Commanders cannot be assigned to Subservient Units.
Small Arms Weapons and Weapons of E2 or lower which target this Infantry Unit must use their 2nd range value.

During this Unit’s activation, it may launch one Squad of X Units of Y. Follow the usual Disembarking rules, treating this Unit as their Transport. Each launched Squad joins this Unit’s Group. This Unit may not launch if 2 Y Squads are already in its Group. If this Unit is destroyed, all Y Squads in its Group are destroyed. At the start of this Unit’s Group’s activation, you may destroy any number of Y Squads in this Group.

This Squad gains +2DF in CQBs. In addition, per Squad with two or more Guard Units in a CQB, one friendly Squad of your choosing without Guard gains +2DF for that CQB, assigned at the start of step 1 of that CQB. If both players have Units with Guard and/or Strong, the player without the Initiative selects all Squads to affect with these abilities first.
This Squad may not be taken in your Army.

children.heading: When one Squad shares multiple identical Transports, those Transports form a Squad. Do they need to maintain coherency?

runs.t: Yes, those Transports must maintain coherency with each other but not with the Squad they are carrying.

children.heading: Can multiple Squads share multiple Transports, provided all Squads and Transports share a single larger Transport? E.g., can three Squads of two Legionnaire Units each share two Bear APCs, which in turn share a Condor Dropship?

runs.t: No. Multiple Squads can only share one larger non-Auxiliary “top-level” Transport. Each Squad in the Group must be either directly embarked in the larger Transport, or embarked in and filling a Squad of Transports that are in turn embarked in the larger transport.

children.heading: Can a Squad embark into any Transport in the Group, or only the Transport(s) it was assigned to during Group formation? E.g, I have two Squads of Legionnaires (A and B) embarked in two Bears (C and D respectively). If Bear C is destroyed, can Legionnaires A embark into Bear D?

runs.t: Squads are assigned to specific Transports when building an army, but during a game, they may embark into any eligible Transports in the same Group. In the example, Legionnaires A can embark into Bear D, despite having started the game in Bear C. Similarly, if a third Bear (E) were reassigned to the Group due to Bear C being destroyed, Legionnaires A or B could embark into Bear E.

children.heading: Can multiple transports together carry a single larger unit? E.g. can three Neptune Dropships carry a single Hades?

runs.t: No. A Unit must entirely fit inside a Transport in order to embark into it.

children.heading: For determining if a Transport can be reassigned to a Group, do Auxiliary Transports in that group count when determining if the Group has sufficient Transports?

runs.t: Yes.

children.heading: How does Infiltrate work with a Squad Deploying via Infiltrate when they have a Transport without Infiltrate? E.g. a Squad of Longreach Snipers Infiltrating, plus their Juno.

runs.t: The Squad Deploys via Infiltrate.Their Transport begins empty and Ready, even if it would ordinarily have to start Reserved due to not being an Aircraft or not having Strike.

children.heading: What if the Transport is embarked in another Transport? E.g. two Squads of Longreach Snipers Infiltrating, plus their two Junos and a Neptune.

runs.t: The Squad Deploys via Infiltrate. Their Transport begins empty and Ready, Embarked in its Transport that also begins Ready. There are no non-Transport Squads in this Group without Infiltrate, so this is allowed.

children.heading: What if the Transport (either the Transport belonging to the Infiltrators or the “top level” Transport it is Embarked in) is an Auxiliary Transport? E.g. a Squad of Longreach Snipers plus their pair of Angelos Jetskimmers.

runs.t: Only non-Auxiliary Transports of Infiltrating Squads may begin empty and Ready. Auxiliary Transports need to either Infiltrate as well via their own Infiltrate rule, or they prevent all Squads in their Group from entering via Infiltrate.

children.heading: What if any non-Transport Units in the Group do not have Infiltrate? E.g a Squad of Longreach Snipers Infiltrating, plus their Juno, a Squad of Immortals in their own Juno, both in a Neptune.

runs.t: In order for any Squads in a Group to Infiltrate, all Squads must either have Infiltrate and deploy via it, or be non-Auxiliary Transports. As one or more non-Transport Squads in the Group do not have Infiltrate (the Immortals), no Squads in the Group may Infiltrate.

children.heading: How do Auxiliary Transports work when sharing one larger Transport? Are they treated as Squads or as Transports?

runs.t: Auxiliary Transports are treated as Squads when forming Groups, so count toward the maximum of 4 Squads sharing one large Transport in a Group. E.g. Two Squads of two UCM Troop Buggies, one carrying two Legionnaires and the other carrying two Hazard Suits, all embarked in a Vulture Dropship would be four Squads sharing one large transport, so would be allowed.

children.heading: Can multiple Squads form a Group Embarked in a single Squad of Auxiliary Transports, which is then Embarked in multiple identical Transports (a “Group 3” style Group from page 10 of the Rulebook)?

runs.t: Multiple Squads can be taken with and share a single Auxiliary Transport Squad, even if that Auxiliary Transport Squad has multiple Units, unlike normal Transports. However, that Auxiliary Transport Squad may only then either have no Transport/s itself or be taken in a single Transport (either on its own or sharing with other Squad/s).

For example, two Legionnaires and two Hazard Suits may embark in and share a Squad of four Troop Buggy Auxiliary Transports. Those Buggies may then either be taken with no Transports or taken in a single Vulture Dropship. They may not be taken in and split across a pair of Raven Light Dropships, as this breaks the “ONE larger transport” rule (since those auxiliary Transport Troop Buggies count as a regular Squad).

children.heading: In 2.2 Placing Units, what is meant by Units “overlapping?” Can units share a footprint if they physically fit? E.g. Can a Shaltari Grav-Tank be placed between the legs of a Warstrider?

runs.t: Yes. Overlapping refers to units physically overlapping. For example, a walker’s leg placed on top of a tank. If models can be positioned so that they physically fit, such as the example of a tank sitting between the legs of a taller model, this is allowed. Note that models must be placed stably, realistically, and with all points of contact (e.g legs, tank treads) in contact with the Table.

For Vehicle models supplied with bases, or where a player has added a base, the base is ignored in the same way as with Aircraft. Other Units may be placed on these bases. Other Units may not overlap with Infantry Units’ bases though, since the base is part of an Infantry Unit.

children.heading: Can a Unit enter the table via the Jump rule?

runs.t: Yes. The Unit is able to Jump when it starts moving, and Units Entering the Table start their movement as they Enter it.

children.heading: How does Movement work for Squads of multiple Units?

runs.t: One Unit at a time, move every Unit within the Squad up to its maximum Mv, or if it has attacked this Round, the lowest MA of any Weapon it attacked with. When the Squad has finished moving, all Units in the Squad must be in Coherency. At that point the Squad completes its Move.

children.heading: In 6.1 Moving, the rules say that Units may turn freely but pivoting on the spot counts as moving 1”. Does this mean that every pivot during a movement uses 1” of Mv?

runs.t: No. This is regarding the MA (Move and Attack Limit) of Weapons. Pivoting on the spot but not actually moving is treated as making a 1” move for the purpose of Weapons with limited MA, such as MA 0”.

children.heading: If a Squad cannot end their movement in Coherency, must they instead end as close as possible to being in Coherency?

runs.t: No. The Units are not compelled to move closer to each other unless they are able to move back into Coherency, in which case they must do so. Note however that a Squad out of coherency cannot attack, Embark, or Disembark.

children.heading: How does Disembarking during a Transport’s movement work?

runs.t: During movement, place the Transport where it would be if it ended its movement there. Then Disembark any disembarking Units. Then complete the Transport’s movement. Note that this means Transports cannot Disembark Units from a place where the Transport cannot be placed legitimately.

children.heading: Can a Group benefit from a Status Token placed during its own attack? E.g., can a Squad attacking with a Jammer Weapon place and benefit from the increased range of the Jammer Weapon for other Units attacking in the Group at the same time?

runs.t: No. Attacks from a Group are simultaneous, and any Status Tokens placed by that attack do not take effect until after the attack is completed.

children.heading: Can you attack with a Weapon with Assault / attack when Disembarking from a Transport with Strike in the same activation in which you Embark into a Transport Unit?

runs.t: No. A Unit cannot attack in the Round in which it Embarks into a Transport Unit, regardless of whether it has Assault or if the Transport it is Disembarking from has Strike.

children.heading: Can a Squad with MA 0” Weapons that have Assault, or are Disembarking from a Transport with Strike, attack with those Weapons after Disembarking?

runs.t: No. Strike grants Disembarking Units Assault on their Weapons, and Assault states that if a Unit with an Assault Weapon Disembarks and moves 0”, it counts as having moved 1” for attacking purposes.

children.heading: Can a weapon with CC range be used to attack Sited Infantry if the attacking Unit is in physical contact with the face of the building or the point on the Area where the infantry are Sited? And can the Weapon attack the Zone?

runs.t: CC weapons can be used to attack the Zone, but not the Infantry Sited in the Zone directly - They would be scattered across multiple floors.

children.heading: How does Strafe interact with targeting Zones and/or Squads in Zones?

runs.t: When targeting Squads in an Area, you may split your attacks if the next Squad is Sited at a point within 3” of where the previously targeted Squad was Sited.

When targeting Squads in a Building, you may split your attacks if the next Squad may be targeted using a point within 3” of the point where you targeted the previous Squad. For example, if you target a Squad on a face using its central door, you may target another Squad on that face using that same door, or another door/window within 3” of it. You may also target a Squad on a different face providing it has a window/door within 3” of the window/door you used to target the previous Squad.
Seeker and Flame Weapons may target Infantry ‘as if they were Sited anywhere on a Zone’, so they may split their attacks freely between any Occupiers in that Zone if that Weapon also has Strafe.
Strafe does not allow splitting attacks against Zones themselves, so a Strafe Weapon must put all its attacks into one Zone, or none.

children.heading: How does Strafe work with Small Arms Weapons? Can I allocate Small Arms shots to multiple Units via Strafe, then choose to combine them or not combine them individually?

runs.t: Yes. Combining fire via Small Arms is decided after allocating Weapons to targets or, in the case of Strafe, after allocating individual attacks. You are therefore able to allocate your Small Arms attacks from a Strafe Weapon to multiple Units, then choose to combine or not per target attacked by that Weapon. Note that all targets must still be in arc, range, and Line of Sight.

children.heading: And can Small Arms Weapons with Pen X+ or Destroyer X+ inflict damage on non Infantry without combining?

runs.t: No. The rule states, ‘They can only damage Infantry’, so Pen X+ and Destroyer X+ would inflict no damage. Once combined, though, they can damage non-Infantry, so Pen X+ and Destroyer X+ could then take effect.

children.heading: Can Small Arms Weapons place Status tokens with regular attacks or only when they combine?

runs.t: Small Arms weapons that place Status tokens can place them using non-combined attacks since placing a Status token is not inflicting damage.

children.heading: If Drive-By is used, what is the position of the other Units in the Squad for Line of Sight when the attack is made?

runs.t: Drive-By is used after the Squad completes its movement, so all Units in the Squad are in the position they finished the movement in. Drive-By then allows the attacking Units to draw line of sight and range from a point along their own movement for their attacks, checked individually per attacking Unit. Therefore, Drive-By Units do not normally interfere with each other’s Line of Sight unless it is drawn through where they ended their move.

children.heading: Is an AA-S or AA-R Weapon an AA weapon (for the purposes of Field or any other mechanics that refer to AA Weapons)?

runs.t: Yes. An AA-S or AA-R Weapon is still an AA weapon and is treated as having the Anti Air special rule, with the additions and exceptions granted by AA-S and AA-R.

children.heading: How do Articulated and Large interact?

runs.t: Large states that you use the Weapon’s pivot point or the base of the barrel to determine the range and Line of Sight from a Weapon. Articulated then lets you determine Line of Sight from 1” above that point (unlike on non-Large Units, where it allows you to determine Line of Sight from 1” above the centre of the model).

children.heading: Do Weapons with Devastator inflict additional damage to Infantry?

runs.t: No. Devastator weapons inflict additional DP when rolling to inflict damage against Units, and you do not roll to inflict damage against Infantry.

children.heading: How do multiple Reaction Attacks work?

runs.t: Multiple Weapons may Reaction Attack the same Aircraft—declare and resolve each individually, so if you’re unsuccessful, you can attack with the next qualifying Weapon. The next Weapon must target the same point or a point further along that Aircraft’s movement.
The aircraft is treated as being at that point when the Reaction Attack is made for Line of Sight range, where it crashes if applicable, AWACS, and so on.

children.heading: How do Reaction Attacks and Jump interact? Can an AA and an Overwatch weapon both Reaction Attack a jumping Unit?

runs.t: An AA Weapon may Reaction Attack the Jump Unit at any point in its movement as if it were an Aircraft, provided it is in range, arc and Line of Sight of the Weapon at that point.
An Overwatch weapon may Reaction Attack the Jump Unit, treating it as a Vehicle making a 0” move at its final position.

children.heading: How do Reaction Attacks and Fast Movers Flying High interact? Can an AA weapon Reaction Attack a Fast Mover as it begins to Fly High, and/or when it stops Flying High?

runs.t: If the Fast Mover began its move Flying High, an AA Weapon could only Reaction Attack it right at the end of its move IF it elects to return to normal height (the rest of its move would have been flying high). If the Fast Mover elected to fly high at the end of its move, it could be Reaction Attacked at any point it moved along (it would have been at normal height throughout that move).

children.heading: How does strafe and Reaction Attack work? Can I walk my shots onto a Unit I’m not Reaction Attacking? Or do I fire the entire gun at the same unit?

runs.t: Strafe has no effect when the Weapon attacks its Unit’s activation, so all the Weapon’s attacks would target the Unit being Reaction Attacked.

children.heading: Can a single Squad suffer cumulative -1DF penalties from multiple Strong Squads in a CQB?

runs.t: Yes.

children.heading: In what order are Strong, Guard and First Strike resolved if both players have access to these abilities in a CQB?

runs.t: First Strike takes place at the start of a CQB, before Step 1, so before Strong or Guard are applied. Strong and/or Guard are applied by the player without the Initiative first, at the start of step 1 of the CQB. Their opponent then applies Strong and/or Guard.

children.heading: Do Concussed Infantry Squads with First Strike X reduce X by half?

runs.t: Concussed Infantry Squads cannot use First Strike at all, as only non-Sited Squads may inflict hits via First Strike, and Concussed treats the Infantry Squad as being Sited for CQBs.

children.heading: 8.7 Close Quarter Battle says that Infantry may voluntarily fail their Bravery test without rolling, even if they have more than half their Units remaining. They can only attempt the Bravery test if they are below half strength, however. Can they still attempt and then voluntarily fail the Bravery test?

runs.t: Yes. This rule allows them to attempt and fail the Bravery test without rolling, even if they would otherwise not be able to attempt the test.

children.heading: If an Infantry Squad starts and ends their Activation in a contested Zone, and they have a Status Token(s) received prior to their Activation, what happens first - the removal of their Status Token(s) or the CQB?

runs.t: The CQB takes place first, then after it is fully resolved any Status Tokens that would be removed are removed. This means that Concussed or Jammed Squads remain Concussed or Jammed throughout the CQB.

children.heading: What comes first, “end of the End Phase” or “end of the Round?”

runs.t: The end of the End Phase happens first and is then followed by the End of the Round. This means that Command Cards played at the end of the End Phase are played before players spend remaining CP on Plan (which happens at the end of the Round).

children.heading: Is the 2+ to find an object via Mapping Tokens modifiable, e.g. would enemy Occupiers with Terror worsen that to a 3+?

runs.t: Yes, the 2+ replaces the base 6+ / 5+ required, and is modifiable.

children.heading: If a Living Weapons Squad forms one Squad with another Living Weapons Squad in the Initiation Phase, and one of them has a Status token, what happens?

runs.t: The new Squad gains any Status Tokens any contributing Squads had. Duplicate Tokens are discarded.

children.heading: Do Units with Bikes count as Vehicles or Infantry for Scenario Objectives? And for Bioficer Decon weapons, do they count as Infantry or as Vehicles for RM generation?

runs.t: Bikes outside Zones count as Vehicles for Scenario Objectives. However, they are treated as Infantry for Decon weapons.

children.heading: Aux Gates cannot be targeted by Command Cards that target Gates. Can they be targeted by cards that target non-Gates?

runs.t: Yes.
